children.title: Interval Newton Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes producing weak, inconclusive, or unstable Newton verification.

children.title: Rank-Deficient Conditioning Regimes
children.top_down_role: Verification difficulties associated with rank loss and severe conditioning.

children.title: Singular Interval Systems
children.top_down_role: Verification behavior when rank loss occurs within the enclosed system family.

knowledge_statements.title: Singular Interval Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of regularity in the interval linear systems underlying an interval Newton step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An interval matrix \(\boldsymbol A\subseteq\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is singular when it contains at least one singular point matrix: \[\exists A\in\boldsymbol A\quad\det A=0.\] For an interval right-hand side \(\boldsymbol b\), the united solution set is \(\Sigma(\boldsymbol A,\boldsymbol b)=\{x:Ax=b,\ A\in\boldsymbol A,\ b\in\boldsymbol b\}\). If \(\boldsymbol A\) is singular, a uniformly bounded inverse enclosure for all members does not exist; \(\Sigma\) may be unbounded or empty for some realizations. Therefore an interval Newton operator requiring inversion of every \(A\in\boldsymbol A\) cannot yield its usual regularity-based existence or uniqueness certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If an interval matrix contains a singular member, uniform inversion fails and regular interval Newton verification is unavailable.
assumptions_latex: \(\boldsymbol A\) is a compact interval matrix.
Interval Newton verification is formulated through uniform solution enclosure over all \(A\in\boldsymbol A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Containment of a singular point matrix blocks any certificate that depends on uniform invertibility of \(\boldsymbol A\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: An authoritative interval-linear-algebra source is required. Many references distinguish an interval matrix that contains a singular member as nonregular rather than simply singular. The discussion also conflates the united solution set with empty or unbounded solution sets of individual realizations.

children.title: Nearly Singular Interval Systems
children.top_down_role: Weak contraction and sensitivity under severe but nonzero conditioning.

knowledge_statements.title: Nearly Singular Interval Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative inverse sensitivity when an interval matrix is regular but approaches rank loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\boldsymbol A\subseteq\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be a compact regular interval matrix and define \[\delta=\min_{A\in\boldsymbol A}\sigma_{\min}(A)>0.\] Then \(\sup_{A\in\boldsymbol A}\|A^{-1}\|_2=1/\delta\). For \(Ax=b\), first-order perturbations obey \[\|\delta x\|_2\leq\delta^{-1}\bigl(\|\delta b\|_2+\|\delta A\|_2\|x\|_2\bigr)+o(\|\delta A\|_2+\|\delta b\|_2).\] Hence small positive \(\delta\) amplifies interval widths and rounding errors; verification can fail numerically even though every member of \(\boldsymbol A\) remains nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regular interval system becomes verification-sensitive as its smallest attainable singular value approaches zero.
assumptions_latex: \(\boldsymbol A\) is compact and every \(A\in\boldsymbol A\) is nonsingular.
The spectral norm is used.
Perturbations are sufficiently small for the first-order estimate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The worst-case inverse norm equals \(1/\delta\), so enclosure sensitivity diverges as \(\delta\downarrow0\).

notation.meaning: Minimum singular-value margin over the interval matrix.
Smallest singular value of a point matrix.
Spectral matrix norm or Euclidean vector norm.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inverse-norm identity is standard for a compact regular family, but the first-order estimate needs a defined nominal system, perturbation model, and sourced remainder conditions. As a leaf under failure boundaries, failure_boundary is more exact than property.

children.title: Rank-Loss Localization
children.top_down_role: Regional identification of possible rank deficiency within search boxes.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Loss Localization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branch-and-bound localization of parameter boxes that may contain a singular matrix realization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a parameter box \(X_0\) and an interval enclosure \(J(X)\supseteq\{J(x):x\in X\}\), initialize a queue with \(X_0\). For each box \(X\), compute a certified lower bound \(\underline\sigma(X)\leq\min_{x\in X}\sigma_{\min}(J(x))\). Discard \(X\) when \(\underline\sigma(X)>0\). Otherwise, if \(\operatorname{diam}(X)\leq\varepsilon\), retain \(X\) as unresolved; if not, bisect it and enqueue its children. The output union contains every \(x\in X_0\) satisfying \(\operatorname{rank}J(x)<n\). Boxes with positive lower bounds are certified rank-loss-free; retained boxes are enclosures, not existence certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bisect parameter space, discard boxes with certified positive minimum singular value, and retain small unresolved boxes enclosing all possible rank-loss points.
assumptions_latex: \(J:X_0\to\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is continuous.
Every computed \(\underline\sigma(X)\) is a rigorous lower bound.
Bisection covers each parent box exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The retained boxes cover \(\{x\in X_0:\operatorname{rank}J(x)<n\}\), although a retained box need not contain rank loss.

notation.meaning: Interval enclosure of the matrix-valued map on a box.
Certified lower bound on the smallest singular value.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The covering logic is plausible under rigorous singular-value lower bounds, but no source or construction for such bounds is supplied. A sourced algorithm must also specify finite termination and treatment of boxes at the tolerance threshold.

children.title: Conditioning-Sensitive Verification
children.top_down_role: Certificate behavior across varying levels of numerical conditioning.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditioning-Sensitive Verification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A perturbation-aware condition preserving a strict interval Newton inclusion certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N\) be the exact interval Newton image and \(\widehat N\) its computed enclosure. Suppose a verified error bound gives \(N\subseteq\widehat N+B_ho\), where \(B_ho=\{z:\|z\|\leq\rho\}\). Define the computed inclusion margin \[m=\inf_{y\in\widehat N}\operatorname{dist}(y,\mathbb R^n\setminus X).\] If \(m>\rho\), then \(N\subseteq\operatorname{int}X\), so the corresponding interval Newton existence conclusion remains valid. When linear-solve analysis yields \(\rho\leq\gamma\eta\), with perturbation size \(\eta\) and conditioning factor \(\gamma\), the checkable sufficient condition is \(m>\gamma\eta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Verification survives computed error when the strict inclusion margin exceeds the conditioning-amplified error bound.
assumptions_latex: \(N\subseteq\widehat N+B_ho\) is rigorously established.
Distances and set enlargements use the same norm.
The applicable interval Newton inclusion theorem holds for the exact image \(N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m>\rho\), or sufficiently \(m>\gamma\eta\), guarantees \(N\subseteq\operatorname{int}X\).

notation.meaning: Distance margin from the computed image to the exterior of the box.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The margin argument is mathematically plausible, but the relationship between the exact and computed images, the certified radius, and the method-dependent factor gamma requires an authoritative validated-error-analysis source and explicit definitions.

children.title: Non-Simple Root Isolation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Persistent boxes and weak isolation near non-simple roots.

children.title: Multiple-Root Verification
children.top_down_role: Certification difficulties near roots lacking local simplicity.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiple-Root Verification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verification by deflating a prescribed multiplicity structure into a regular augmented system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be sufficiently differentiable and let \(x^*\) be a suspected non-simple zero. Construct an augmented deflated system \(G(z)=0\), with \(z=(x,\lambda)\), such that solutions of \(G\) project to zeros of \(F\), the auxiliary equations encode the claimed multiplicity structure, and \(G'(z^*)\) is nonsingular at the corresponding solution. If an interval Newton test on a box \(Z=X\times\Lambda\) proves \[N_G(\hat z,Z)\subseteq\operatorname{int}Z,\] then \(Z\) contains a unique augmented solution and \(X\) contains its projected zero. The claimed multiplicity is certified only when equivalence of the deflation equations to that multiplicity has also been established.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deflation can convert a multiple root into a regular augmented root; interval inclusion then verifies it, provided the deflation equations certify multiplicity.
assumptions_latex: The deflated system is differentiable and regular at the augmented root.
Every augmented solution projects to a zero of \(F\).
The auxiliary equations are proved equivalent to the claimed multiplicity structure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strict interval Newton inclusion for \(G\) certifies one augmented solution and its projected multiple root in \(X\).

notation.meaning: Interval Newton image for the augmented system.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement is too scheme-independent to certify a multiple root. A concrete deflation construction, explicit smoothness order, regularity hypotheses for its interval Jacobian, and a theorem connecting the auxiliary equations to the claimed multiplicity are required.

children.title: Root-Cluster Isolation
children.top_down_role: Persistent uncertainty when several roots remain enclosed by one region.

knowledge_statements.title: Root-Cluster Isolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Univariate complex root-cluster isolation by a validated argument-principle count.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\) be a complex polynomial and let \(D\subset\mathbb C\) be a bounded region with positively oriented piecewise-smooth boundary \(\Gamma\). Suppose validated complex interval evaluation proves \(0\notin p(\Gamma)\) and encloses \[k=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_\Gamma\frac{p'(z)}{p(z)}\,dz\] in an interval containing exactly one integer \(k\). Then \(D\) contains exactly \(k\) zeros of \(p\), counted with multiplicity. If validated exclusion also proves that a surrounding annulus contains no zero, \(D\) is an isolated root cluster separated from all remaining roots.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A validated argument-principle count plus a root-free surrounding annulus certifies an isolated polynomial root cluster of known total multiplicity.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) has no zero on \(\Gamma\).
The contour integral is enclosed with outward-rounded validated arithmetic.
The optional separation claim uses a certified root-free surrounding annulus.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The region contains exactly \(k\) roots counted with multiplicity and, with annular exclusion, forms an isolated cluster.

notation.meaning: Positively oriented boundary of the region.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The candidate is an argument-principle certificate for univariate complex polynomials, not an interval Newton failure-boundary statement. It does not fit this terminal container within the Interval Newton Family, irrespective of its validity in a separate root-counting context.

children.title: Multiplicity-Sensitive Contraction
children.top_down_role: Changes in local contraction quality associated with root multiplicity.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplicity-Sensitive Contraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar contraction after regularizing a known-multiplicity root through a removable quotient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:I\to\mathbb R\) have a root \(r\) of known multiplicity \(m\geq2\), and suppose \(u(x)=f(x)/f'(x)\) admits a continuously differentiable extension through \(r\). Define \(g(x)=m u(x)\); then \(g(r)=0\) and \(g'(r)=1\). For a box \(X\subset I\), choose \(\hat x\in X\), compute interval extensions \(G(\hat x)\ni g(\hat x)\) and \(G'(X)\supseteq g'(X)\), and set \[N_m(\hat x,X)=\hat x-G(\hat x)/G'(X),\qquad X^+=X\cap N_m(\hat x,X).\] If \(0\notin G'(X)\), every root of \(g\) in \(X\) is retained; strict inclusion gives the usual simple-root verification for the regularized equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For known multiplicity, regularize the Newton quotient and contract the resulting simple-root equation with validated interval arithmetic.
assumptions_latex: The multiplicity \(m\) is known and \(u=f/f'\) has a differentiable removable extension at the root.
The interval extensions enclose \(g\) and \(g'\) on \(X\).
\(0\notin G'(X)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X^+=X\cap N_m(\hat x,X)\) retains every regularized root in \(X\); strict interior inclusion verifies one.

notation.meaning: Regularized function with a simple root.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The local identity for m f/f' is plausible near a root of known multiplicity, but a source must establish the removable extension, its valid neighborhood, and the validated interval construction. Strict inclusion verifies a root of the regularized equation; additional localization is needed to associate it with the prescribed multiple root.

children.title: Cluster-Separation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Resolution limits governing whether nearby roots can be certified separately.

assumptions_latex: \(0<\varepsilon\in\mathbb{R}\)
\(f_\varepsilon(x)=x^2-\varepsilon^2\) on \(X=[-2\varepsilon,2\varepsilon]\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in f_\varepsilon'(X)\), so the classical interval Newton step cannot separate the roots \(-\varepsilon\) and \(\varepsilon\) without subdivision or a multiplicity-aware representation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar boundary illustrating failure of simple-root interval Newton separation.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f_\varepsilon(x)=x^2-\varepsilon^2\), the interval \(X=[-2\varepsilon,2\varepsilon]\) contains the distinct roots \(-\varepsilon\) and \(\varepsilon\), whose separation is \(2\varepsilon\). Since \(f_\varepsilon'(X)=2X=[-4\varepsilon,4\varepsilon]\) contains zero, division by the interval derivative in the classical interval Newton map is unbounded or undefined. Consequently, a simple-root Newton inclusion test on \(X\) cannot certify two disjoint root enclosures. Separation requires subdivision into boxes excluding zero from their derivative images, or a representation explicitly adapted to multiple roots or clusters.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two roots closer than the current box scale can force the derivative enclosure through zero, preventing classical interval Newton separation until subdivision or specialized treatment.
knowledge_statements.title: Cluster-Separation Boundaries

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

children.title: Newton Representation Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Weak contraction caused by unsuitable local representations.

children.title: Poor Newton Centers
children.top_down_role: Weak local representations caused by unsuitable evaluation centers.

assumptions_latex: \(F:X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is continuously differentiable
\(\bar x\in X\) and \(C\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A large residual term \(CF(\bar x)\) can prevent \(K(\bar x,X)\subseteq X\) even when the linear remainder is contractive.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-induced failure of a centered, preconditioned Newton representation.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \([F'(X)]\) enclose every Jacobian on \(X\), and define \(K(\bar x,X)=\bar x-CF(\bar x)+(I-C[F'(X)])(X-\bar x)\). Its displacement from \(\bar x\) contains the residual contribution \(-CF(\bar x)\). Even if the remainder matrix satisfies \(\lVert I-C[F'(X)]\rVert<1\) in an induced interval norm, a center having sufficiently large \(\lVert CF(\bar x)\rVert\) may place \(K(\bar x,X)\) outside \(X\). Thus contractivity of the linear remainder alone does not imply a validating inclusion; the center must also control the preconditioned residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A center with a large preconditioned residual can make the Newton enclosure leave the box despite a contractive linear remainder.
knowledge_statements.title: Poor Newton Centers

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

children.title: Poor Newton Preconditioners
children.top_down_role: Weak or unstable contraction caused by unsuitable preconditioning matrices.

assumptions_latex: \(F(x)=Ax-b\) with nonsingular \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\)
\(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is a nondegenerate box and \(\bar x\in X\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\lVert I-CA\rVert\ge 1\), the preconditioned Newton representation need not reduce the radius of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear model exposing loss of contraction from inaccurate preconditioning.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the affine system \(F(x)=Ax-b\), the Krawczyk enclosure is \(K(\bar x,X)=\bar x-C(A\bar x-b)+(I-CA)(X-\bar x)\). Its radius obeys the componentwise identity \(\operatorname{rad}(K)=|I-CA|\operatorname{rad}(X)\). Hence a preconditioner for which \(I-CA\) is not contractive can preserve or enlarge box widths, independently of the center residual. In particular, \(C=0\) gives \(K(\bar x,X)=X\), while an approximation \(C\approx A^{-1}\) is useful only to the extent that it makes \(I-CA\) small.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A poor approximate inverse leaves a large remainder matrix, so the preconditioned Newton enclosure may preserve or enlarge the box.
knowledge_statements.title: Poor Newton Preconditioners

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

children.title: Center–Preconditioner Interaction
children.top_down_role: Coupled effects of center placement and preconditioner choice on verification strength.

knowledge_statements.title: Center–Preconditioner Interaction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint inclusion criterion for the center and point preconditioner.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r=CF(\bar x)\), let \(\mathcal R=\{I-CJ:J\in[F'(X)]\}\), and define \(K(\bar x,X)=\bar x-r+\mathcal R(X-\bar x)\). For an induced norm, set \(q=\sup_{R\in\mathcal R}\lVert R\rVert\) and \(\rho=\sup_{x\in X}\lVert x-\bar x\rVert\). Then \(\sup_{y\in K(\bar x,X)}\lVert y-\bar x\rVert\le\lVert r\rVert+q\rho\). Hence the center and preconditioner interact through the combined residual and remainder bound: changing \(\bar x\) changes \(r\) and \(\rho\), while changing \(C\) changes both \(r\) and \(q\). If \(d=\inf_{z\in\partial X}\lVert z-\bar x\rVert\) and \(\lVert r\rVert+q\rho<d\), then \(K(\bar x,X)\subset\operatorname{int}(X)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The validating inclusion depends jointly on the preconditioned center residual, the preconditioned Jacobian remainder, and the center's position in the box. A sufficient condition is that their combined norm bound fit strictly inside the distance from the center to the box boundary.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is continuously differentiable on an open neighborhood of a box \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\)
\(\bar x\in\operatorname{int}(X)\), \(C\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), and \([F'(X)]\) encloses every Jacobian \(F'(x)\) for \(x\in X\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\lVert r\rVert+q\rho<d\), then \(K(\bar x,X)\subset\operatorname{int}(X)\).

notation.meaning: set of preconditioned Jacobian remainder matrices
remainder bound, centered box radius, and distance to the boundary

children.title: Adaptive Representation Recovery
children.top_down_role: Alternative local representations used after weak contraction is detected.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Representation Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive recovery by recentering, repreconditioning, and eventual subdivision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a queue with \(X_0\). For each extracted box \(X_k\), choose a center \(\bar x_k\in X_k\) and a nonsingular point preconditioner \(C_k\), preferably using an approximate Newton point and an approximate inverse of \(\operatorname{mid}([F'(X_k)])\). Form \(K_k=\bar x_k-C_kF(\bar x_k)+(I-C_k[F'(X_k)])(X_k-\bar x_k)\). Exclude \(X_k\) if \(K_k\cap X_k=\varnothing\), and record a validated root enclosure if \(K_k\subset\operatorname{int}(X_k)\). Otherwise replace \(X_k\) by \(K_k\cap X_k\) when this gives sufficient contraction, then recenter or recompute \(C_k\). After a prescribed number of unsuccessful recovery attempts, bisect the current box. Terminate when the queue is empty or when a prescribed width or finite work limit is reached, retaining any unclassified boxes as unresolved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each candidate box, adapt the center and nonsingular approximate inverse, exclude or validate when the Krawczyk tests succeed, contract when useful, and subdivide after repeated recovery failures. A finite stopping rule may leave a list of unresolved boxes.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is continuously differentiable on an open neighborhood of the initial box \(X_0\subset\mathbb R^n\)
Validated interval evaluations of \(F\) and \(F'\) are available
Every Krawczyk inclusion test uses a nonsingular point matrix \(C_k\)
A finite work limit or termination tolerance is prescribed
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure produces finite collections of validated root enclosures, excluded boxes, and any boxes unresolved at the prescribed stopping limit.

notation.meaning: Krawczyk enclosure for the current representation

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

children.title: Finite-Precision Newton Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Loss of effective contraction near representational limits.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Precision Newton Stagnation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-point stagnation caused by outward-rounded representable endpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N_{\mathbb F}(X)\) be a deterministic, outward-rounded interval Newton update intersected with the current box \(X\). Finite-precision Newton stagnation occurs when \(N_{\mathbb F}(X)=X\), so repeating the same evaluation with the same precision and representation reproduces the same endpoints. In particular, endpoint improvements of the corresponding real-arithmetic update can disappear when they are smaller than the spacing to adjacent representable endpoints. If \(\operatorname{wid}(X)>\tau\), identical repetitions cannot attain the requested tolerance \(\tau\); progress requires a changed representation, increased precision, or subdivision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deterministic outward-rounded Newton update stagnates when it reproduces the current representable box. If that box is wider than the requested tolerance, repeating the identical computation cannot finish the enclosure.
assumptions_latex: All finite interval endpoints belong to a floating-point set \(\mathbb F\)
Every interval operation uses outward rounding
\(N_{\mathbb F}\) is evaluated deterministically with fixed precision and a fixed representation
\(\tau\ge0\) is the requested width tolerance
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(N_{\mathbb F}(X)=X\) and \(\operatorname{wid}(X)>\tau\), further identical evaluations cannot establish width at most \(\tau\).

children.title: Validated Infeasibility Certificate
children.top_down_role: Box-level evidence that no feasible point is present.

children.title: Direct Constraint-Range Infeasibility
children.top_down_role: Infeasibility certified from objective-independent constraint images.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is a box
Feasibility requires \(g_i(x)\le0\) and \(h_j(x)=0\)
\(G_i(X)\supseteq g_i(X)\) and \(H_j(X)\supseteq h_j(X)\) are validated enclosures
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If some \(\inf G_i(X)>0\) or some \(0\notin H_j(X)\), then \(X\) contains no feasible point.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-independent infeasibility from one validated constraint image.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each inequality constraint, let \(G_i(X)\) be a validated interval containing \(\{g_i(x):x\in X\}\); for each equality constraint, define \(H_j(X)\) analogously. If \(\inf G_i(X)>0\) for at least one \(i\), every point of \(X\) violates that inequality. If \(0\notin H_j(X)\) for at least one \(j\), no point of \(X\) satisfies that equality. Either condition is therefore a directly checkable certificate that \(X\cap\mathcal F=\varnothing\), independent of objective values or incumbent bounds, where \(\mathcal F\) is the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A box is infeasible when one inequality enclosure lies strictly above zero or one equality enclosure excludes zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Direct Constraint-Range Infeasibility

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

children.title: Empty-Contractor Infeasibility
children.top_down_role: Infeasibility certified by complete contraction of a candidate box.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is the feasible set
\(C\) is a validated contractor satisfying \(X\cap\mathcal F\subseteq C(X)\subseteq X\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C(X)=\varnothing\) certifies \(X\cap\mathcal F=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infeasibility certificate supplied by a solution-preserving contractor.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A validated contractor for the feasible set \(\mathcal F\) is a mapping satisfying \(X\cap\mathcal F\subseteq C(X)\subseteq X\) for every input box \(X\). The first inclusion is the solution-preservation requirement: no feasible point in \(X\) may be removed. Consequently, if validated contraction produces \(C(X)=\varnothing\), then \(X\cap\mathcal F\subseteq\varnothing\), and hence \(X\cap\mathcal F=\varnothing\). The empty contracted image is therefore a verifiable infeasibility certificate, provided all contractor arithmetic and logical constraint reductions used to obtain emptiness are inclusion-valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a solution-preserving validated contractor reduces a box to the empty set, the original box contains no feasible point.
knowledge_statements.title: Empty-Contractor Infeasibility

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

children.title: Inequality Inner Feasibility
children.top_down_role: Boxes certified to satisfy inequality constraints throughout.

knowledge_statements.title: Inequality Inner Feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Whole-box inner certificate for non-strict inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\in\mathbb N\), let \(\mathcal F=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_i(x)\le0\text{ for every }i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\}\), and let each validated interval \(G_i(X)\) contain \(\{g_i(x):x\in X\}\). If \(\sup G_i(X)\le0\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), then every \(x\in X\) satisfies every inequality. Consequently, \(X\subseteq\mathcal F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every validated inequality range over a box is nonpositive, then every point of the box satisfies every inequality, so the whole box is feasible.
assumptions_latex: \(m\in\mathbb N\) and \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a box
Feasibility is defined by \(g_i(x)\le0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\)
\(G_i(X)\supseteq\{g_i(x):x\in X\}\) for every \(i=1,\ldots,m\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\sup G_i(X)\le0\) for every \(i=1,\ldots,m\), then \(X\subseteq\mathcal F\).

notation.meaning: validated enclosure of the ith constraint range

children.title: Equality Feasible-Point Verification
children.top_down_role: Existence-oriented verification for equality-defined feasible sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality Feasible-Point Verification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Square equality system verified by a Krawczyk inclusion test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h:U\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuously differentiable on an open set \(U\) containing a box \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\). For \(\bar x\in X\), a nonsingular matrix \(C\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), and an interval enclosure \([h'(X)]\) of all Jacobians on \(X\), define \(K(\bar x,X)=\bar x-Ch(\bar x)+(I-C[h'(X)])(X-\bar x)\). If validated interval arithmetic establishes \(K(\bar x,X)\subset\operatorname{int}(X)\), then there exists at least one \(x^*\in X\) satisfying \(h(x^*)=0\). This is an existence certificate for the equality-defined feasible set; it does not assert that every point of \(X\) is feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a square continuously differentiable equality system and a nonsingular point preconditioner, strict Krawczyk inclusion certifies at least one feasible zero in the box, not whole-box feasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a box contained in an open set \(U\)
\(h:U\to\mathbb R^n\) is continuously differentiable
\(\bar x\in X\), \(C\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is nonsingular, and \([h'(X)]\) encloses every \(h'(x)\) for \(x\in X\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(K(\bar x,X)\subset\operatorname{int}(X)\), then there exists \(x^*\in X\) such that \(h(x^*)=0\).

children.title: Indeterminate Feasibility-Box Regimes
children.top_down_role: Boxes unresolved near constraint boundaries or singular feasible sets.

children.title: Boundary Feasibility Boxes
children.top_down_role: Boxes intersecting or closely tracking certified constraint boundaries.

knowledge_statements.title: Boundary Feasibility Boxes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computational boundary classification, not a certificate of actual boundary intersection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\in\mathbb N\), let \(\mathcal F=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_i(x)\le0\text{ for every }i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\}\), and let \(G_i(X)\) be a validated enclosure of \(\{g_i(x):x\in X\}\). Under direct range classification, call \(X\) a boundary feasibility box when \(\inf G_i(X)\le0\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) and at least one \(k\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) satisfies \(\inf G_k(X)\le0<\sup G_k(X)\). Thus no direct range test proves infeasibility, while at least one constraint range prevents whole-box feasibility certification. This classification indicates possible intersection with \(\partial\mathcal F\), but interval overestimation means it does not certify an actual boundary point in \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A boundary feasibility box passes every direct range-exclusion test but has at least one constraint enclosure straddling zero. It may meet the feasible-set boundary, although the range test alone does not prove that it does.
assumptions_latex: \(m\in\mathbb N\) and \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a candidate box
Feasibility is defined by \(g_i(x)\le0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\)
\(G_i(X)\supseteq\{g_i(x):x\in X\}\) for every \(i=1,\ldots,m\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The direct range tests classify \(X\) as boundary-indeterminate when every \(\inf G_i(X)\le0\) and at least one \(G_k(X)\) straddles zero.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

children.title: Undecided Feasibility Boxes
children.top_down_role: Boxes lacking sufficient evidence for feasible or infeasible classification.

knowledge_statements.title: Undecided Feasibility Boxes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual classification state after all currently selected validated tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the full feasible set, including every applicable equality and inequality constraint, and let \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a candidate box. Relative to a specified family of sound validated tests, call \(X\) undecided when no applied test certifies \(X\cap\mathcal F=\varnothing\) and no applied test certifies either \(X\subseteq\mathcal F\) or the existence of a point \(x^*\in X\cap\mathcal F\), according to the positive classification being sought. Any existential certificate must validate all constraints defining \(\mathcal F\), not merely an equality subsystem. Undecided status records insufficiency of the selected enclosures, contractors, and existence tests; it does not imply that both feasible and infeasible points occur in \(X\). The box must be refined, tested more strongly, or retained as unresolved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A box is undecided when the selected sound tests prove neither infeasibility nor the applicable positive feasibility claim. Any claimed feasible point must satisfy the complete constraint system, and undecided status does not imply mixed feasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is the full feasible set and \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a candidate box
A specified family of sound validated infeasibility and feasibility tests has been applied
Any existential feasibility test checks every constraint defining \(\mathcal F\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the applied tests certify neither \(X\cap\mathcal F=\varnothing\) nor the applicable positive feasibility claim, then \(X\) remains undecided.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

children.title: Singular Feasible-Set Regimes
children.top_down_role: Classification behavior near lower-dimensional or singular feasible structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Singular Feasible-Set Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LICQ-based singularity for equality and active-inequality constraints inside an interval box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the feasible set be \(F=\{x\in X:g_i(x)\leq 0,\ i=1,\ldots,m,\ h_j(x)=0,\ j=1,\ldots,p\}\), where the constraints are continuously differentiable. For \(x\in F\), let \(I(x)=\{i:g_i(x)=0\}\) and let \(A(x)\) have rows \(\nabla h_j(x)^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\nabla g_i(x)^{\mathsf T}\) for \(i\in I(x)\). A singular feasible-set regime occurs when some \(x\in F\) satisfies \(\operatorname{rank}A(x)<p+|I(x)|\). At such a point, feasibility classifiers whose certification requires LICQ or a nonsingular implicit-function Jacobian have no applicable regularity certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point is singular when its equality and active-inequality gradients are linearly dependent; classifiers requiring regular constraint Jacobians then cannot certify its local geometry.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty box.
\(g_i,h_j\in C^1\) on a neighborhood of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}A(x)<p+|I(x)|\) prevents certification by feasibility tests requiring LICQ or Jacobian nonsingularity.

notation.meaning: feasible subset of the current box
indices of inequalities active at x
Jacobian of equality and active-inequality constraints

review_flags: Exact interval-classification treatment of singular active sets requires an authoritative source.
Distinguish failure of a regularity certificate from proof of infeasibility.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The LICQ rank condition is standard, but failure of the combined active-constraint rank does not by itself rule out every implicit-function Jacobian certificate. An authoritative source must identify the exact interval classifier and regularity condition intended.

children.title: Persistent Classification Ambiguity
children.top_down_role: Uncertainty that remains under contraction, refinement, or finite-precision evaluation.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Classification Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ambiguity persisting along a nested sequence of validated feasibility boxes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C(B)\in\{\mathrm{in},\mathrm{out},\mathrm{undetermined}\}\) be a sound interval feasibility classifier for boxes \(B\subset X\). A point \(x^*\in X\) exhibits persistent classification ambiguity if there is a nested sequence \(B_1\supset B_2\supset\cdots\) with \(x^*\in B_k\), \(\operatorname{diam}(B_k)\to0\), and \(C(B_k)=\mathrm{undetermined}\) for every \(k\). Thus refinement along this sequence never produces a validated inside or outside classification, even though the boxes converge to the singleton \(\{x^*\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ambiguity is persistent when arbitrarily small nested boxes around a point remain formally undetermined under a sound feasibility classifier.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) never labels a box inside or outside unless the corresponding inclusion or exclusion claim is valid.
\(B_k\) are nonempty closed boxes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C(B_k)=\mathrm{undetermined}\) for all \(k\) despite \(\bigcap_{k\geq1}B_k=\{x^*\}\).
review_flags: Needs a source fixing the intended interval-classifier semantics.
Definition does not assert that every refinement strategy remains ambiguous.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is internally precise and correctly concerns one nested refinement sequence, but the intended three-valued interval-classifier semantics lack source support.

children.title: Natural-Extension Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Bounds obtained directly from natural interval objective enclosures.

knowledge_statements.title: Natural-Extension Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower endpoint of an inclusion interval produced by the natural extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be represented by a finite expression, and let \(F\) be its natural interval extension obtained by replacing each real operation and elementary function by an inclusion interval counterpart. For every box \(X\) contained in the expression domain, the inclusion property of interval evaluation gives \(f(X)=\{f(x):x\in X\}\subseteq F(X)\). Consequently, if \(F(X)=[\underline F(X),\overline F(X)]\), then \(L_N(X)=\underline F(X)\) is a validated lower bound satisfying \(L_N(X)\leq\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lower endpoint of a natural interval evaluation is a certified lower bound for every objective value in the box.
assumptions_latex: Every interval operation used in \(F\) encloses the range of its real counterpart.
\(X\) lies within the common domain of the expression and its interval extension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_N(X)=\underline F(X)\leq\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: natural interval enclosure of the objective on X

children.title: Derivative-Enhanced Local Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Derivative-enhanced lower bounds localized to a search region.

children.title: Centered Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Localized lower bounds built around a selected center.

knowledge_statements.title: Centered Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order centered-form enclosure evaluated about a point in the box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in C^1(X)\), choose \(c\in X\), and let \(G_i(X)\) enclose \(\{\partial_i f(x):x\in X\}\). The centered mean-value form is \(M_c(X)=f(c)+\sum_{i=1}^nG_i(X)(X_i-c_i)\), with all operations evaluated by outward-rounded interval arithmetic. The multivariate mean-value theorem implies \(f(X)\subseteq M_c(X)\). Hence the lower endpoint \(L_C(X;c)=\underline{M_c(X)}\) satisfies \(L_C(X;c)\leq\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\), and is therefore a validated derivative-enhanced lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expanding at a box point and enclosing every first derivative yields a centered interval whose lower endpoint safely bounds the box minimum.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a convex box and \(c\in X\).
\(G_i(X)\supseteq\{\partial_i f(x):x\in X\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_C(X;c)=\underline{M_c(X)}\leq\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: interval enclosure of the ith partial derivative

children.title: Slope-Based Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Regional lower bounds using finite-region slope information.

knowledge_statements.title: Slope-Based Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower bound from interval slopes relative to a fixed expansion point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(c\in X\). Suppose intervals \(S_i(X,c)\) have the slope property that, for every \(x\in X\), there exist \(s_i\in S_i(X,c)\) satisfying \(f(x)-f(c)=\sum_{i=1}^ns_i(x_i-c_i)\). Define the slope enclosure \(E_S(X;c)=f(c)+\sum_{i=1}^nS_i(X,c)(X_i-c_i)\) using outward-rounded interval arithmetic. Then \(f(X)\subseteq E_S(X;c)\), so \(L_S(X;c)=\underline{E_S(X;c)}\) is a validated lower bound on \(f\) over \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interval slopes enclosing every exact displacement quotient produce an objective enclosure whose lower endpoint certifies the box minimum.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a box and \(c\in X\).
The stated slope property holds for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_S(X;c)=\underline{E_S(X;c)}\leq\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: interval slope enclosure in coordinate i

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

children.title: Taylor Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Higher-order localized lower bounds using validated remainder information.

knowledge_statements.title: Taylor Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order interval Taylor enclosure about a point in the box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in C^2(X)\), choose \(c\in X\), and let \(H_{ij}(X)\) enclose every Hessian entry \(\partial_{ij}f(x)\) on \(X\). Define \(T_2(X;c)=f(c)+\nabla f(c)^{\mathsf T}(X-c)+\tfrac12(X-c)^{\mathsf T}H(X)(X-c)\), interpreting the quadratic expression by outward-rounded interval arithmetic. Taylor's theorem with remainder gives \(f(X)\subseteq T_2(X;c)\). Therefore \(L_T(X;c)=\underline{T_2(X;c)}\) is a validated lower bound for the objective on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A second-order Taylor form with an interval Hessian encloses all box values, so its lower endpoint is a certified bound.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a convex box and \(c\in X\).
\(H_{ij}(X)\supseteq\{\partial_{ij}f(x):x\in X\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_T(X;c)=\underline{T_2(X;c)}\leq\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\).

children.title: Derivative-Enhanced Bound Selection

knowledge_statements.title: Derivative-Enhanced Bound Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe selection among finitely many validated derivative-based lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a box \(X\), an expansion point \(c\in X\), and successfully computed validated bounds \(L_C(X;c)\), \(L_S(X;c)\), and \(L_T(X;c)\); unavailable bounds are omitted. Initialize \(L=-\infty\), then update \(L\leftarrow\max\{L,L_j(X;c)\}\) for each available candidate \(j\in\{C,S,T\}\). Output \(L_D(X)=L\). If at least one candidate is available and every candidate satisfies \(L_j(X;c)\leq\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\), then \(L_D(X)\) is valid and dominates every selected candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute available validated derivative bounds and retain their maximum; the result remains valid and is never weaker than any selected bound.
assumptions_latex: Every admitted candidate \(L_j(X;c)\) is a validated lower bound on the same box.
At least one candidate bound is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_D(X)=\max_jL_j(X;c)\leq\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\) and \(L_D(X)\geq L_j(X;c)\) for every selected \(j\).

notation.meaning: an available validated candidate lower bound

children.title: Monotonicity Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Bounds strengthened through certified coordinate monotonicity.

knowledge_statements.title: Monotonicity Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact face reduction from certified coordinatewise derivative signs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\prod_{i=1}^n[a_i,b_i]\) and let \(G_i(X)\) enclose \(\partial_i f(X)\). Form the face \(X^M\) by fixing coordinate \(i\) to \(a_i\) when \(\underline{G_i(X)}\geq0\), fixing it to \(b_i\) when \(\overline{G_i(X)}\leq0\), and leaving it unchanged otherwise. Coordinatewise monotonicity then yields \(\inf_{x\in X}f(x)=\inf_{x\in X^M}f(x)\). Consequently, the lower endpoint of any validated enclosure of \(f(X^M)\) is a valid monotonicity-strengthened lower bound on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified derivative signs move minimization to the corresponding lower or upper box faces, where any validated enclosure supplies a lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(G_i(X)\supseteq\{\partial_i f(x):x\in X\}\) for every coordinate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in X}f(x)=\inf_{x\in X^M}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: interval enclosure of the ith partial derivative
face obtained from certified monotonicity signs

children.title: Curvature-Based Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Lower bounds using validated second-order shape information.

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Based Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic lower model from a certified uniform Hessian eigenvalue bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in C^2(X)\), choose \(c\in X\), and suppose validated spectral analysis proves \(\nabla^2f(x)\succeq\mu I\) for every \(x\in X\), where \(\mu\in\mathbb R\) may be negative. Then Taylor's theorem gives \(f(x)\geq q_\mu(x)=f(c)+\nabla f(c)^{\mathsf T}(x-c)+\tfrac\mu2\lVert x-c\rVert_2^2\) for all \(x\in X\). Thus \(L_\mu(X;c)=\min_{x\in X}q_\mu(x)\), computed with validated arithmetic, certifies \(L_\mu(X;c)\leq\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified lower eigenvalue bound for every Hessian produces a quadratic underestimator whose box minimum is a valid objective lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a compact convex box and \(c\in X\).
\(\nabla^2f(x)\succeq\mu I\) for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_\mu(X;c)=\min_{x\in X}q_\mu(x)\leq\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: certified uniform lower bound on Hessian eigenvalues
minimum of the underestimator over X

children.title: Convexity-Based Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Lower bounds exploiting certified convex behavior over a search region.

knowledge_statements.title: Convexity-Based Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine tangent lower bound under validated convexity on the box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in C^1(X)\) be convex on a compact box \(X=\prod_{i=1}^n[a_i,b_i]\), and choose \(c\in X\). The supporting-hyperplane inequality gives \(f(x)\geq f(c)+\nabla f(c)^{\mathsf T}(x-c)\) for every \(x\in X\). Therefore the affine bound \(L_{\mathrm{cvx}}(X;c)=f(c)+\sum_{i=1}^n\min\{\partial_i f(c)(a_i-c_i),\partial_i f(c)(b_i-c_i)\}\) satisfies \(L_{\mathrm{cvx}}(X;c)\leq\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\). Convexity may be certified by proving \(\nabla^2f(x)\succeq0\) throughout \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Validated convexity makes every tangent plane a global underestimator; minimizing that affine function over the box gives a certified lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable and convex on \(X\).
Values and derivatives entering the formula are evaluated with validated arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_{\mathrm{cvx}}(X;c)\leq\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: box minimum of the tangent affine underestimator

children.title: Indefinite-Curvature Regimes
children.top_down_role: Bound behavior when Hessian enclosures do not certify a uniform curvature sign.

knowledge_statements.title: Indefinite-Curvature Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of tangent-plane lower bounds when convexity certification is absent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(X=[-1,1]^2\), consider \(f(x_1,x_2)=x_1^2-x_2^2\). Its Hessian is \(\nabla^2f=\operatorname{diag}(2,-2)\), so the curvature is indefinite everywhere. At \(c=(0,0)\), the tangent model equals \(f(c)+\nabla f(c)^{\mathsf T}(x-c)=0\), but \(f(0,1)=-1<0\); hence that tangent model is not a lower bound. Nevertheless, the certified eigenvalue bound \(\mu=-2\) gives the valid curvature model \(q_{-2}(x)=-x_1^2-x_2^2\leq f(x)\) on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An indefinite quadratic shows that a tangent plane need not underbound a nonconvex objective, while a negative certified curvature bound still yields a safe model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The tangent model at \((0,0)\) is invalid as a lower bound, whereas \(q_{-2}(x)\leq f(x)\) on \(X\).

notation.meaning: quadratic model formed with the Hessian lower bound minus two

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: all claims follow by direct evaluation of the displayed quadratic and its constant Hessian.

children.title: Curvature-Certificate Quality

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Certificate Quality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordering curvature lower bounds by their certified Hessian eigenvalue constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(X\), \(c\in X\), and the quadratic models \(q_\mu(x)=f(c)+\nabla f(c)^{\mathsf T}(x-c)+\tfrac\mu2\lVert x-c\rVert_2^2\). If two certified constants satisfy \(\mu_1\leq\mu_2\leq\inf_{x\in X}\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x))\), then \(q_{\mu_1}(x)\leq q_{\mu_2}(x)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). Consequently, their box minima obey \(L_{\mu_1}(X;c)\leq L_{\mu_2}(X;c)\leq\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\). Thus a larger valid curvature constant gives a certificate at least as strong.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Among valid Hessian lower bounds, the larger constant produces a pointwise tighter quadratic underestimator and therefore a no-worse box lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(f\in C^2(X)\) and \(X\) is a compact convex box.
\(\mu_1\leq\mu_2\) are validated uniform Hessian eigenvalue lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_{\mu_1}(X;c)\leq L_{\mu_2}(X;c)\leq\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: smallest eigenvalue of a symmetric matrix
quadratic model using curvature constant mu
minimum of the curvature model on X

children.title: Hybrid Interval–Relaxation Bounds
children.top_down_role: Validated bounds combining interval information with linear, convex, or dual relaxations.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Interval–Relaxation Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certified lower bounds obtained by intersecting interval and relaxation information on one search box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a box and let \(F_X=[\underline f_I,\overline f_I]\) be an outward-rounded interval enclosure of \(f(X)\). Suppose a linear, convex, or dual relaxation valid for every feasible \(x\in X\) has optimal value \(\underline f_R\), so that \(\underline f_R\le f(x)\). Then \[L_X=\max\{\underline f_I,\underline f_R\}\] is a validated lower bound for the objective over the feasible part of \(X\). If a validated incumbent upper bound \(U\) satisfies \(L_X>U\), the box contains no improving feasible point and may be discarded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximum of a rigorous interval lower bound and any valid relaxation lower bound remains rigorous and can certify pruning against an incumbent.
assumptions_latex: \(f(X)\subseteq F_X\) is computed with outward rounding.
\(\underline f_R\le f(x)\) for every feasible \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_X\le \inf\{f(x):x\in X\text{ feasible}\}\), and \(L_X>U\) certifies exclusion.

notation.meaning: interval enclosure of the objective range on the box

children.title: Validated Point-Value Incumbents

knowledge_statements.title: Validated Point-Value Incumbents
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A certified feasible point and an outward objective evaluation furnish a rigorous incumbent bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the feasible set for a minimization problem. Suppose \(\hat x\in S\) has been certified feasible, including all equality and inequality constraints, and an outward-rounded evaluation gives \(f(\hat x)\in F(\hat x)=[\underline u,\overline u]\). Then \(U=\overline u\) is a validated upper bound on the global minimum \(f^*=\inf_{x\in S}f(x)\). Among several certified points, the minimum of their validated upper endpoints is again a validated incumbent upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The upper endpoint of an outward objective enclosure at a certified feasible point is a rigorous upper bound on the minimum.
assumptions_latex: \(S\ne\varnothing\) and \(\hat x\in S\) is certified.
\(f(\hat x)\in[\underline u,\overline u]\) under outward rounding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f^*\le f(\hat x)\le U=\overline u\).

knowledge_statements.title: Verified Feasible-Neighborhood Incumbents
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A nonempty region certified feasible supports an upper bound through an interval enclosure of its objective range.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty box or validated neighborhood satisfying \(N\subseteq S\), where \(S\) is the feasible set. If outward-rounded evaluation yields \(f(N)\subseteq[\underline u_N,\overline u_N]\), then every \(x\in N\) is feasible and satisfies \(f(x)\le\overline u_N\). Consequently \(U_N=\overline u_N\) is a validated incumbent upper bound for \(f^*=\inf_{x\in S}f(x)\). The certificate must include both verified nonemptiness and verified containment in \(S\); an objective range enclosure alone does not certify an incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A verified nonempty feasible neighborhood and its outward objective enclosure provide a rigorous incumbent through the enclosure’s upper endpoint.
assumptions_latex: \(\varnothing\ne N\subseteq S\).
\(f(N)\subseteq[\underline u_N,\overline u_N]\) is outwardly enclosed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f^*\le U_N=\overline u_N\).

children.title: Local-Solver-Assisted Incumbents
children.top_down_role: Validated use of candidates produced by nonvalidated local optimization.

knowledge_statements.title: Local-Solver-Assisted Incumbents
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonvalidated local solutions become incumbents only after independent validation of feasibility and objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the feasible set of a minimization problem, let \(f^*=\inf_{x\in S}f(x)\), and let \(U_{\rm old}\) be a validated upper bound satisfying \(f^*\le U_{\rm old}\). Given a box \(X\), run any local solver to obtain a candidate \(x^{\rm loc}\). Construct either a representable point \(\hat x\) or a nonempty validated neighborhood \(N\ni x^{\rm loc}\), and independently verify either \(\hat x\in S\) or \(N\subseteq S\), respectively. Using outward rounding, compute an interval enclosure \(F(\hat x)\ni f(\hat x)\) in the point case or \(F(N)\supseteq f(N)\) in the neighborhood case. Set \(U=\sup F(\hat x)\) or \(U=\sup F(N)\), as applicable, only after feasibility validation succeeds. Then update \(U_{\rm new}=\min\{U_{\rm old},U\}\); if either validation fails, retain \(U_{\rm new}=U_{\rm old}\). Every accepted update satisfies \(f^*\le U_{\rm new}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local solver only proposes candidates. Independently validated feasibility and an outward objective enclosure determine whether a candidate may improve the rigorous incumbent.
assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is the feasible set and \(f^*=\inf_{x\in S}f(x)\).
\(U_{\rm old}\) is a validated upper bound on \(f^*\).
Constraint and objective validations use outward-rounded enclosures.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f^*\le U_{\rm new}\) after every accepted or rejected candidate update.

children.title: Monotonicity Tests
children.top_down_role: Coordinatewise shape tests supporting exclusion and face reduction.

knowledge_statements.title: Monotonicity Tests
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivative-sign enclosures certify coordinate monotonicity and reduce minimization to a boundary face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\prod_{j=1}^n[a_j,b_j]\) and let \(f\) be continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of \(X\). If an interval derivative enclosure satisfies \(D_i(X)\supseteq\{\partial_i f(x):x\in X\}\) and \(\inf D_i(X)>0\), then \(f\) is strictly increasing in coordinate \(i\), so every minimizer on \(X\) lies on \(x_i=a_i\). If \(\sup D_i(X)<0\), every minimizer lies on \(x_i=b_i\). In either case, \(X\) contains no interior stationary point and may be replaced by the certified minimizing face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A derivative interval strictly on one side of zero certifies monotonicity and moves all box minimizers to the appropriate boundary face.
assumptions_latex: \(f\in C^1\) on a neighborhood of \(X\).
\(D_i(X)\) encloses \(\partial_i f\) throughout \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf D_i(X)>0\Rightarrow x_i=a_i\), while \(\sup D_i(X)<0\Rightarrow x_i=b_i\), for every box minimizer.

notation.meaning: interval enclosure of the ith partial derivative

children.title: Validated Convexity Tests

knowledge_statements.title: Validated Convexity Tests
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-semidefiniteness of every matrix in an interval Hessian certifies convexity on a convex box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) be convex and let \(f\in C^2\) on a neighborhood of \(X\). Let \(\mathcal H(X)\) be a symmetric interval-matrix enclosure satisfying \(\nabla^2f(x)\in\mathcal H(X)\) for every \(x\in X\). If a validated matrix test proves \(d^{\mathsf T}Hd\ge0\) for every \(H\in\mathcal H(X)\) and every \(d\in\mathbb R^n\), then \(f\) is convex on \(X\). Strict positivity for every nonzero \(d\), uniformly over \(\mathcal H(X)\), certifies strict convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every Hessian represented by a validated interval enclosure is positive semidefinite, the objective is certified convex on the box.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is convex and \(f\in C^2\) near \(X\).
\(\nabla^2f(x)\in\mathcal H(X)\) for all \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal H(X)\succeq0\Rightarrow f\) is convex on \(X\).

notation.meaning: symmetric interval enclosure of all Hessians on the box
a point matrix represented by the interval Hessian

children.title: Validated Nonconvexity Tests

knowledge_statements.title: Validated Nonconvexity Tests
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A certified negative-curvature direction at one interior point disproves convexity on the containing convex region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be convex with nonempty interior, and let \(f\in C^2\) on a neighborhood of \(X\). Suppose a certified point \(x_0\in\operatorname{int}X\), a vector \(d\in\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}\), and an outward-rounded interval \(Q\) satisfy \(d^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2f(x_0)d\in Q\) and \(\sup Q<0\). Then \(\nabla^2f(x_0)\) is not positive semidefinite, so \(f\) is not convex on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rigorously negative Hessian quadratic form at a certified interior point proves that the function is not convex on the containing convex region.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is convex with nonempty interior, \(x_0\in\operatorname{int}X\), and \(f\in C^2\) near \(X\).
\(d\in\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}\).
\(Q\) outwardly encloses \(d^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2f(x_0)d\) and satisfies \(\sup Q<0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is not convex on \(X\).

notation.meaning: validated enclosure of the Hessian quadratic form

children.title: Gradient-Zero Filters
children.top_down_role: Stationarity exclusion for interior minimizer candidates.

knowledge_statements.title: Gradient-Zero Filters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An interval gradient component excluding zero rules out stationary points in the search box interior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a box and let \(f\in C^1\) on a neighborhood of \(X\). For each coordinate, let \(G_i(X)\) enclose \(\{\partial_i f(x):x\in X\}\). If \(0\notin G_i(X)\) for at least one \(i\), then no point in \(X\) satisfies \(\nabla f(x)=0\). Hence \(X\) contains no unconstrained interior local minimizer. In a box-constrained search, the whole box may be discarded only if boundary minimizers are handled separately; otherwise the result justifies reduction to boundary faces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If any enclosed gradient component excludes zero, the box has no stationary point and no unconstrained interior minimizer.

\(\partial_i f(X)\subseteq G_i(X)\) for every tested coordinate.

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Face Stationarity Filters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order box optimality conditions are tested on each candidate active face using validated derivative enclosures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\prod_{i=1}^n[a_i,b_i]\) and let a face \(F\) fix indices in \(L\) at lower bounds and indices in \(U\) at upper bounds, leaving indices in \(J\) free. A local minimizer in the relative interior of \(F\) must satisfy \(\partial_jf(x)=0\) for \(j\in J\), \(\partial_if(x)\ge0\) for \(i\in L\), and \(\partial_if(x)\le0\) for \(i\in U\). If validated derivative enclosures on \(F\) make any required equality or sign impossible, then the relative interior of \(F\) contains no box-constrained local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A face is excluded when interval derivatives cannot satisfy zero conditions on free coordinates and the required one-sided signs on fixed coordinates.

Derivative intervals enclose every partial derivative on \(F\).

children.top_down_role: Multiplier-system filtering in regimes supported by suitable constraint qualifications.

knowledge_statements.title: KKT-System Filters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validated infeasibility of the KKT system excludes local minimizers whenever an applicable constraint qualification guarantees KKT necessity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m,p\in\mathbb N_0\), and consider minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(g_i(x)\le0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\) and \(h_j(x)=0\) for \(j=1,\ldots,p\), where \(f\), every \(g_i\), and every \(h_j\) are continuously differentiable near a candidate box \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\). Suppose a constraint qualification guaranteeing KKT necessity holds at every feasible local minimizer in \(X\). The KKT system is \[
abla f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i
abla g_i(x)+\sum_{j=1}^p
u_j
abla h_j(x)=0,\qquad g_i(x)\le0,\qquad h_j(x)=0,\qquad \lambda_i\ge0,\qquad \lambda_i g_i(x)=0,\] with \(x\in X\), \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\), and \(
u\in\mathbb R^p\), where the indexed conditions hold for all applicable \(i\) and \(j\). If validated interval solving proves that this system has no solution in \(X	imes\mathbb R_+^m	imes\mathbb R^p\), then \(X\) contains no constrained local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a constraint qualification makes KKT conditions necessary, rigorous infeasibility of the complete primal-multiplier KKT system over a box certifies that the box contains no constrained local minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(m,p\in\mathbb N_0\), and \(f,g_i,h_j\) are continuously differentiable near \(X\).
A constraint qualification ensuring KKT necessity holds at every feasible local minimizer in \(X\).
Validated solving covers all \((x,\lambda,\nu)\in X\times\mathbb R_+^m\times\mathbb R^p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Validated KKT infeasibility implies that \(X\) contains no constrained local minimizer.

children.title: Fritz–John-System Filters
children.top_down_role: Multiplier-system filtering that also covers degenerate constrained regimes.

assumptions_latex: \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m,h_1,\ldots,h_p\) are continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of a box \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\).
The feasible set is \(F=\{x\in X:g_i(x)\le 0,\ h_j(x)=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the normalized Fritz--John system has no solution over \(B\), then \(B\) contains no local minimizer in the relative interior of \(X\).

notation.meaning: active inequality index set at x

review_flags: exact interval-system implementation requires source confirmation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized Fritz--John exclusion without a constraint qualification; bound-active variants require corresponding normal-cone terms.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Basic Concepts of Global Optimization p. 33

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every local minimizer \(x^*\in F\) lying in the relative interior of \(X\), there exist multipliers \(\alpha\ge 0\), \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\), and \(\mu\in\mathbb R^p\), not all zero, satisfying \[\alpha
abla f(x^*)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i
abla g_i(x^*)+\sum_{j=1}^p\mu_j
abla h_j(x^*)=0,\qquad \lambda_i g_i(x^*)=0.\] Multipliers may be normalized by \(\alpha+\sum_i\lambda_i+\sum_j|\mu_j|=1\). Thus a validated solver may reject \(B\subseteq X\) when interval evaluation proves that feasibility, complementarity, stationarity, and normalization have no simultaneous solution in \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A box is safely rejected when validated computation excludes every normalized Fritz–John point, including abnormal points with zero objective multiplier.
knowledge_statements.title: Fritz–John-System Filters

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Basic Concepts of Global Optimization p. 33

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role and normalized Fritz–John exclusion claim fit the leaf, but the cited locator begins a chapter with convex sets and does not specifically support the Fritz–John theorem or its validated interval-system implementation. A source locator for the Fritz–John necessary conditions and normalization is required.

assumptions_latex: \(f\) and all selected active constraint functions are continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of \(B\subset\mathbb R^n\).
A candidate active set contains active nonlinear constraints and active lower or upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every local minimizer consistent with the selected active set satisfies the reduced stationarity equation \(Z(x)^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(x)=0\) together with the active constraints.

notation.meaning: vector of selected active nonlinear and bound constraints
Jacobian of the selected active constraints
basis matrix for the null space of the active Jacobian

review_flags: reduced-space interval formulation requires source confirmation

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Basic Concepts of Global Optimization p. 33

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an active-set hypothesis \(A\) and suppose \(J_A(x)\) has constant full row rank on \(B\). Let the columns of \(Z(x)\) span \(\ker J_A(x)\). The active-set first-order system can then be represented as \[c_A(x)=0,\qquad Z(x)^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(x)=0,\] supplemented by feasibility of every inactive inequality and the sign conditions on multipliers when those multipliers are recovered. A validated exclusion of this reduced system over \(B\), for every active-set hypothesis compatible with \(B\), excludes constrained stationary minimizers from \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each possible active set, stationarity is projected onto feasible tangent directions; excluding every resulting reduced system excludes constrained stationary minimizers.
knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Space Active-Constraint Systems
