children.title: Validated Multiplier Bounds
children.top_down_role: Certified multiplier ranges used to strengthen optimality systems and regional bounds.

assumptions_latex: A constrained first-order system is valid on \(B\), and interval operations use outward rounding.
Every multiplier enclosure is proved to contain all multipliers associated with candidate minimizers in \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Intersecting the optimality system with validated multiplier boxes preserves every candidate minimizer and can certify exclusion when the strengthened interval system is empty.
review_flags: specific multiplier-bounding construction requires source confirmation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soundness condition for using certified multiplier enclosures in interval optimality filters.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S(B)\) denote all pairs \((x,y)\) satisfying the chosen first-order necessary conditions with \(x\in B\). A box \(Y(B)\) is a validated multiplier bound when \[S(B)\subseteq B\times Y(B).\] Consequently, replacing an unrestricted multiplier domain by \(Y(B)\), or intersecting an existing enclosure with \(Y(B)\), cannot remove any multiplier pair associated with a candidate minimizer. If outward-rounded interval evaluation or a validated equation solver proves \(S(B)\cap(B\times Y(B))=\varnothing\), then \(B\) contains no minimizer governed by that necessary system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified multiplier intervals safely tighten constrained optimality systems; if the tightened system is empty, the candidate box can be rejected.
knowledge_statements.title: Validated Multiplier Bounds

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate is conditionally sound once Y(B) is proved to enclose all relevant multipliers, and its content kind fits the leaf. The cited general interval-methods section does not inspectably support validated multiplier enclosures or a construction establishing that premise.

children.title: Box-Reduction Families
children.top_down_role: Solution-preserving mechanisms that shrink an optimization search region.

children.title: Constraint-Propagation Reduction
children.top_down_role: Feasible-domain contraction through contractor networks.

assumptions_latex: Each constraint contractor is inclusion-preserving and removes no point satisfying its associated constraint.
All computations on boxes use outward-rounded interval arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The propagated box contains every feasible point of the input box, and an empty propagated box certifies infeasibility.

notation.meaning: feasible set defined by all constraints

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-point propagation by a finite network of sound constraint contractors.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(B^{(0)}\), repeatedly choose a constraint contractor \(C_k\) and set \(B^{(t+1)}=C_k(B^{(t)})\) until a full pass produces no prescribed significant contraction, the box becomes empty, or a resource limit is reached. Soundness requires \[F\cap B\subseteq C_k(B)\subseteq B\] for every box \(B\) and every \(k\). Therefore every iterate satisfies \(F\cap B^{(0)}\subseteq B^{(t)}\). Return the final box as the reduced domain; return infeasible if it is empty, and otherwise branch or apply another validated reduction when propagation stops.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply sound constraint contractors repeatedly. Every feasible point remains, while an empty result is a certificate that the original box is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Propagation Reduction

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

children.title: Objective-Cutoff Reduction
children.top_down_role: Contraction induced by the validated incumbent cutoff.

assumptions_latex: \(U\) is the objective value of a validated feasible incumbent for a minimization problem.
The interval procedure computes an inclusion-preserving lower bound for \(f\) on each tested subbox.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Discarding every subbox \(S\) with \(L(S)>U\), or \(L(S)\ge U\) when ties need not be retained, preserves all improving feasible points.

notation.meaning: certified objective lower bound on S

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization cutoff reduction, with strictness determined by whether equal-valued minimizers must be retained.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition or slice \(B\) into tested subboxes \(S\). For each \(S\), compute by outward-rounded interval methods a number \(L(S)\) satisfying \[L(S)\le \inf\{f(x):x\in S\cap F\}.\] Remove \(S\) whenever \(L(S)>U\). If the task seeks only a point improving the incumbent, remove \(S\) whenever \(L(S)\ge U\). Retain the hull or union of the remaining subboxes and repeat until the contraction tolerance or resource limit is reached. No feasible point with objective below \(U\) is removed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Slices whose certified objective lower bound exceeds the feasible incumbent cannot improve it and may be removed from the search region.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Cutoff Reduction

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

children.title: Interval-Gradient Reduction
children.top_down_role: Domain contraction based on certified gradient information.

assumptions_latex: \(f\) is continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of \(B=\prod_{i=1}^n[a_i,b_i]\).
An interval gradient enclosure \(G_i(B)\) contains \(\partial_i f(x)\) for every \(x\in B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A fixed sign of \(G_i(B)\) moves every minimizer in \(B\) to the corresponding coordinate face, allowing certified deletion of the opposite interior slices.

notation.meaning: interval enclosure of the i-th partial derivative

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-monotonicity reduction for an unconstrained box or a coordinatewise feasible segment.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\inf G_i(B)>0\), then \(f\) is strictly increasing along every coordinate segment \(x+t e_i\) contained in \(B\); hence a minimizer over \(B\) must satisfy \(x_i=a_i\). If \(\sup G_i(B)<0\), a minimizer must satisfy \(x_i=b_i\). Therefore a validated reduction may replace \(B\) by the corresponding face, or delete any boundary slice separated from that face. When \(0\in G_i(B)\), this sign test alone certifies no contraction in coordinate \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A derivative interval strictly on one side of zero proves coordinate monotonicity and confines minimizers to the appropriate box face.
knowledge_statements.title: Interval-Gradient Reduction

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

children.title: Boundary-Slice Reduction Family
children.top_down_role: Coordinate-bound contraction through validated boundary-slice tests.

children.title: Shaving Reduction
children.top_down_role: Coordinate-bound contraction through certified tests on selected boundary slices.

assumptions_latex: A sound rejection test certifies that a tested slice contains no point that must remain in the search.
The candidate box has finite coordinate bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Sequentially deleting certified boundary slices preserves all required solutions and yields a soundly shaved box.

notation.meaning: set of solutions that must be preserved

review_flags: terminology and slice-selection convention require source confirmation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential boundary probing with deletion only after a sound slice-rejection certificate.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize with \(B\). For a selected coordinate \(i\), test the lower slice \(Q^-_i=\{x\in B:a_i\le x_i\le a_i+\delta_i\}\) and the upper slice \(Q^+_i=\{x\in B:b_i-\delta_i\le x_i\le b_i\}\). Delete a slice only when a validated certificate proves \(S\cap Q_i^\pm=\varnothing\), update the corresponding endpoint, and repeat over coordinates until no tested slice is certified removable or a stopping limit is reached. The invariant \(S\cap B^{(0)}\subseteq B^{(t)}\) makes the returned box a sound reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Probe thin boundary slices one at a time and move a box face inward only when that slice is rigorously certified irrelevant.
knowledge_statements.title: Shaving Reduction

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The preservation invariant is sound, and algorithm is the appropriate content kind. The available citation does not inspectably establish that this sequential boundary-slice procedure is the intended meaning of shaving or support its slice-selection convention, so the exact terminal claim requires a source.

children.title: Peeling Reduction
children.top_down_role: Progressive removal of certified boundary layers from a search box.

assumptions_latex: Each boundary-layer rejection test is sound for the solutions that must be preserved.
Layer widths are positive and do not cross the current box.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Removing a certified collection of outer layers preserves every required solution; repeated rounds produce nested sound enclosures.
review_flags: peeling versus shaving convention requires source confirmation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Round-based removal of independently certified outer layers from one or several box faces.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At round \(t\), form finite boundary layers \(Q_1,\ldots,Q_r\subseteq B^{(t)}\) adjacent to selected faces. Validate each rejection using the same pre-round box, collect \(D_t=\bigcup\{Q_k:S\cap Q_k=\varnothing\text{ is certified}\}\), and set \(B^{(t+1)}\) to a box enclosure of \(B^{(t)}\setminus D_t\) that excludes the certified layers. Repeat until no layer is deleted or a stopping rule applies. Since every removed layer is disjoint from \(S\), all iterates satisfy \(S\cap B^{(0)}\subseteq B^{(t)}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Peeling removes a round of certified irrelevant outer layers, then repeats on the smaller box while preserving every required solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Peeling Reduction

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The claimed distinction between peeling and shaving is not supported by the inspectable source. Moreover, existence of a box enclosure of the remainder that excludes every certified layer requires the layers to be full face-adjacent slabs or an equivalent geometric condition, which is not stated. Source confirmation is needed before fixing the intended mathematical version.

children.title: Boundary-Slice Certification
children.top_down_role: Validated evidence supporting removal of tested coordinate slices.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\subseteq B\) is a boundary slice of a current search box \(B\), and \(F\) is the feasible set of a minimization problem with objective \(f\).
\(U\) is the objective value of a validated feasible incumbent, and \(L(Q)\leq\inf\{f(x):x\in Q\cap F\}\) is a certified lower bound whenever the objective alternative is used.

Every interval bound, contractor conclusion, or optimality exclusion used by the certificate is inclusion-preserving; any invoked necessary optimality condition holds for every retained minimizer to which the test is applied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each displayed validated alternative proves \(S_U\cap Q=\varnothing\), where \(S_U=\{x\in B\cap F:f(x)\leq U\}\), so deleting \(Q\) preserves all retained minimizers.

notation.meaning: current search box and tested boundary slice
validated objective lower bound on Q
feasible points in B whose objective is no worse than the incumbent

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Disjunctive certificate supporting deletion of a tested boundary slice while retaining every feasible minimizer whose value is no worse than the incumbent.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(S_U=\{x\in B\cap F:f(x)\leq U\}\). A boundary slice \(Q\) is certified removable if at least one validated alternative holds: \[Q\cap F=\varnothing,\qquad L(Q)>U,\qquad\text{or}\qquad Q\cap F\text{ contains no point satisfying a necessary optimality condition shared by every point of }S_U.\] The first alternative follows from a sound feasibility contractor or interval constraint bound, the second from the certified lower bound \(L(Q)\) and feasible incumbent \(U\), and the third from an applicable validated stationarity or shape exclusion. Each alternative proves \(S_U\cap Q=\varnothing\), thereby justifying deletion of \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A boundary slice can be deleted when certified infeasibility, objective domination, or exclusion of a necessary optimality configuration proves that it contains no feasible minimizer whose value is no worse than the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.title: Boundary-Slice Certification

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

children.title: Reduction-Stagnation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Cases where boundary tests yield insufficient contraction or excessive evaluation cost.

assumptions_latex: A reduction operator \(R\) is sound and contractive: \(S\cap B\subseteq R(B)\subseteq B\).
The implementation declares progress only when width decreases beyond a prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When \(R(B)=B\), or accepted contraction is below tolerance, reduction alone supplies no progress; a sound search may branch, strengthen or change its reduction tests, retain \(B\), or terminate under its stopping policy.

notation.meaning: maximum coordinate width of a box

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational fixed-point and tolerance boundary for sound box-reduction procedures.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Exact stagnation occurs at a nonempty box \(B\) when \(R(B)=B\). Numerical or policy stagnation occurs when \[w(B)-w(R(B))\leq \tau\max\{1,w(B)\}\] for a chosen tolerance \(\tau\geq 0\), although \(R(B)\neq B\). Typical mechanisms include interval overestimation, slices too wide to certify, slices too thin to exceed tolerance, and unresolved constraints or stationarity systems. Soundness is not lost, but repeated application supplies no accepted progress; the search may branch, strengthen bounds, change contractors, retain \(B\), or terminate under its stopping policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduction stagnates at a fixed point or when certified shrinkage is below tolerance; sound search may then branch, strengthen or change its tests, retain the box, or terminate under its stopping policy.
knowledge_statements.title: Reduction-Stagnation Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

children.title: Validated Interval Pruning Certificate
children.top_down_role: Certificate families justifying permanent removal of search regions.

children.title: Objective-Dominance Pruning
children.top_down_role: Rejection based on validated regional lower bounds and an incumbent.

assumptions_latex: \(U\) is attained by a validated feasible incumbent.
\(L(B)\) is a certified lower bound on the objective over all feasible points in \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(L(B)>U\), then \(B\) contains no global minimizer improving or tying the incumbent and may be pruned.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict objective-dominance certificate for retaining all globally optimal ties.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose outward-rounded computation establishes \[L(B)\le \inf\{f(x):x\in B\cap F\}\] and a validated feasible point has objective value \(U\). If \(L(B)>U\), then every feasible \(x\in B\) satisfies \(f(x)>U\); hence no globally minimizing point with value at most \(U\) lies in \(B\), and the box may be discarded. If only improvement over the incumbent is sought, the non-strict test \(L(B)\ge U\) is sufficient, but it may discard distinct minimizers tied at value \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A box is prunable when its certified feasible objective lower bound is worse than the value of a validated feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Dominance Pruning

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

children.title: Constraint-Infeasibility Pruning
children.top_down_role: Rejection based on a validated infeasibility certificate.

assumptions_latex: The feasible set is defined by interval-evaluable equalities, inequalities, and bounds.
Every interval evaluation or contractor used in the certificate is inclusion-preserving.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A validated contradiction for any necessary feasibility condition proves \(B\cap F=\varnothing\), so \(B\) may be pruned.

notation.meaning: interval range enclosure of a constraint on B

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validated infeasibility certificate from interval range exclusion or an empty sound contractor image.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an inequality \(g(x)\le 0\), the condition \(\inf[g](B)>0\) certifies violation throughout \(B\). For an equality \(h(x)=0\), the condition \(0\notin[h](B)\) certifies violation throughout \(B\). More generally, if a sound feasibility contractor \(C_F\) satisfies \(B\cap F\subseteq C_F(B)\subseteq B\) and returns \(C_F(B)=\varnothing\), then \(B\cap F=\varnothing\). Any one of these outward-rounded contradictions is independently checkable and suffices to prune \(B\) without evaluating its objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interval range exclusion or an empty sound feasibility contractor proves that a box contains no feasible point and can be discarded.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Infeasibility Pruning

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

children.title: Stationarity-Exclusion Pruning

Let \(X=\prod_{j=1}^n[\ell_j,u_j]\subset\mathbb R^n\), let \(f\) be continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of \(X\), and let \(G_i(X)\) be a validated enclosure of \(\{\partial_i f(x):x\in X\}\). If \(0
otin G_i(X)\) for some coordinate \(i\), then \(
abla f(x)
e0\) for every \(x\in X\). Consequently, \(X\) contains no unconstrained stationary point and may be removed from a search restricted to interior stationary candidates. This condition alone does not exclude a box-constrained minimizer on \(\partial X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A box contains no stationary point if one validated partial-derivative interval excludes zero; boundary minimizers still require separate treatment.

\(f\in C^1\) on a neighborhood of \(X\).

children.title: Shape-Certified Pruning
children.top_down_role: Rejection or dimension reduction using certified shape information.

children.title: Curvature-Based Pruning
children.top_down_role: Certified rejection of regions using validated shape information.

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Based Pruning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Negative-curvature certificate reducing box minimization to its boundary or vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a compact box and let \(f\in C^2(X)\). Suppose a validated interval Hessian enclosure certifies \(v^{\mathsf T}Hv\le0\) for every \(H\in[\nabla^2 f](X)\) and every \(v\in\mathbb R^n\). Then \(f\) is concave on \(X\), and its minimum over \(X\) is attained at a vertex. Hence the relative interior of \(X\) may be discarded while retaining its vertices, or recursively its proper faces, without changing the global minimum value on the box.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A validated negative-semidefinite Hessian makes the objective concave, so box minimization reduces safely to vertices or boundary faces.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a nonempty compact box.
Every matrix in \([\nabla^2 f](X)\) is negative semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)=\min_{v\in\operatorname{vert}(X)}f(v)\).

notation.meaning: Validated interval enclosure of all Hessians on the box

children.title: Face Pruning
children.top_down_role: Certified rejection or retention decisions restricted to box faces.

knowledge_statements.title: Face Pruning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonicity certificate replacing a box by a lower-dimensional coordinate face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\prod_{j=1}^n[\ell_j,u_j]\) and let \(G_i(X)\) enclose \(\partial_i f(X)\). If \(\inf G_i(X)>0\), define the lower face \(F_i^-:=\{x\in X:x_i=\ell_i\}\). For every \(x\in X\), replacing \(x_i\) by \(\ell_i\) does not increase \(f\), and decreases it when \(x_i>\ell_i\). Thus minimization on \(X\) is equivalent to minimization on \(F_i^-\). If \(\sup G_i(X)<0\), the analogous valid face is \(F_i^+:=\{x\in X:x_i=u_i\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A derivative with certified constant sign forces every box minimizer onto the corresponding lower or upper coordinate face.
assumptions_latex: \(f\in C^1\) on a neighborhood of the box.
\(G_i(X)\) validly encloses \(\partial_i f(x)\) for all \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf G_i(X)>0\Rightarrow\min_X f=\min_{F_i^-}f\), and \(\sup G_i(X)<0\Rightarrow\min_X f=\min_{F_i^+}f\).

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

children.title: Dimension-Reduction Certificates
children.top_down_role: Evidence supporting replacement of a full-dimensional region by relevant faces.

knowledge_statements.title: Dimension-Reduction Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dominance-map certificate reducing minimization from a box to a lower-dimensional subset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) be compact, let \(F\subseteq X\) be compact, and let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) be continuous. A validated map \(P:X\to F\) is a dimension-reduction certificate when \(P(x)=x\) for \(x\in F\) and \(f(P(x))\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). These verifiable relations imply that no point removed from \(X\setminus F\) has a value below all values on \(F\), and therefore the optimization problem may be replaced by its restriction to \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A validated projection onto a lower-dimensional set preserves the minimum when every point is mapped to an equally good or better point.

\(f\) is continuous on \(X\).

knowledge_statements.title: Inconclusive Shape Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary where derivative and curvature enclosures provide no strict pruning certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Shape pruning is inconclusive on a box \(X\) when every validated gradient component contains zero and the interval Hessian enclosure certifies neither the required positive nor negative definiteness. Failure of these tests is not a pruning certificate: the box must remain, be contracted by other information, or be subdivided. For example, for \(f(x)=x^4\) on \(X=[-1,1]\), the enclosures \(f'(X)=[-4,4]\) and \(f''(X)=[0,12]\) neither exclude stationarity nor certify strict curvature, although the box contains the minimizer \(x=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If derivative intervals contain zero and curvature lacks the required strict sign, shape tests cannot justify pruning; subdivision or another certificate is necessary.
assumptions_latex: Gradient and Hessian enclosures are inclusion-valid on \(X\).
No separate dominance, infeasibility, or contraction certificate is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigl(0\in G_i(X)\ \forall i\bigr)\) together with indefinite or non-strict curvature information does not imply that \(X\) is removable.

children.title: Moore–Skelboe Family
children.top_down_role: Objective-enclosure-driven best-bound subdivision methods.

knowledge_statements.title: Moore–Skelboe Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Best-lower-bound interval branch-and-bound using convergent objective enclosures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a compact box \(X_0\), a continuous objective \(f\), an inclusion function \(F\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\). Initialize a queue with \(X_0\) and obtain an incumbent value \(U=f(\hat x)\). Repeatedly select a box \(X\) having minimal lower endpoint \(L(X)=\inf F(X)\); discard it if \(L(X)\ge U-\varepsilon\), otherwise bisect it, evaluate the children, update \(U\) from feasible sampled points, and enqueue unpruned children. Stop when the queue is empty or \(U-\min_XL(X)\le\varepsilon\); output \(\hat x\), \(U\), and the global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method repeatedly subdivides the box with best validated lower bound, updates an incumbent, and stops when the certified optimality gap meets tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(F(X)\supseteq\{f(x):x\in X\}\) for every generated box.
The subdivision rule is exhaustive and reduces box diameters.
Every incumbent value is obtained at a feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U-f^*\le\varepsilon\) at gap termination, where \(f^*=\min_{x\in X_0}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: Validated lower bound for a box

knowledge_statements.title: Contractor-Coupled Global Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validated branch-and-bound interleaving contractors, bounds, incumbents, and subdivision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For constrained minimization of \(f\) over a feasible set \(S\subseteq X_0\), maintain a queue of boxes and a feasible incumbent value \(U\). At a node \(X\), apply a validated contractor \(C\) satisfying \(C(X)\subseteq X\) and \(S\cap X\subseteq C(X)\). Delete the node if \(C(X)=\varnothing\). Otherwise compute a validated lower bound \(L(C(X))\) satisfying \(L(C(X))\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in S\cap C(X)\), delete the node when \(L(C(X))\ge U-\varepsilon\), update \(U\) only from validated feasible points, and bisect every unresolved contracted box. Terminate when every remaining box has lower bound at least \(U-\varepsilon\), or when the queue is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global search safely alternates feasibility-preserving contraction, validated objective bounds, feasible incumbent updates, and subdivision until the certified optimality gap closes.
assumptions_latex: \(X_0\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a compact box and \(S\subseteq X_0\) is the exact feasible set.
\(C\) is contracting and preserves every feasible point in each processed box.
All objective lower bounds and incumbent feasibility checks are validated.
Subdivision is exhaustive for unresolved boxes, and \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U-f^*\le\varepsilon\) at termination, where \(f^*=\min_{x\in S}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: Validated objective lower bound on a box

knowledge_statements.title: Propagation-Aware Node Processing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node-processing loop that propagates constraints and bounds to a validated fixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a box \(Xeing X^{(0)}\), contractors \(C_1,ldots,C_m\), and an incumbent \(U\), repeatedly set \(X^{(k+1)}=C_m\circeingldotseing\circ C_1(X^{(k)})\), interleaving any objective cutoff contractor derived from \(f(x)<U-\varepsilon\). Stop the propagation loop if a box becomes empty, a complete sweep produces no material contraction, or a prescribed safe iteration limit is reached. Recompute validated objective bounds after contraction. Return prune if emptiness or bound dominance is certified; otherwise return the contracted box for incumbent search or subdivision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each node is contracted by repeated constraint and objective-cutoff propagation before bounds are recomputed and pruning or branching is chosen.
assumptions_latex: Each \(C_j\) is contracting and preserves all feasible points.
The objective cutoff contractor preserves every point satisfying \(f(x)<U-\varepsilon\).
Every stopping rule leaves the current outer box inclusion-valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X^{(k+1)}\subseteq X^{(k)}\) and every potentially improving feasible point in \(X\) remains in the returned box.

notation.meaning: Validated contractor in the propagation schedule

children.title: Propagation-Driven Pruning
children.top_down_role: Regional rejection supported by contractor-derived infeasibility or objective reduction.

knowledge_statements.title: Propagation-Driven Pruning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pruning certificate produced by validated constraint and cutoff propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\{x\in X:g_i(x)\le0,h_j(x)=0\}\) be the feasible set in a box, and let \(C_U(X)\subseteq X\) be a validated contractor preserving every \(x\in S\) with \(f(x)<U-\varepsilon\). If propagation yields \(C_U(X)=\varnothing\), then no feasible point in \(X\) can improve the incumbent by more than \(\varepsilon\), so \(X\) is safely prunable. If propagation instead returns \(Y\ne\varnothing\), only \(X\setminus Y\) is certified irrelevant; nonemptiness of \(Y\) does not certify feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An empty improving-point contractor image safely prunes a box; a nonempty image only narrows the search and does not prove feasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is the value of a feasible incumbent.
\(C_U\) preserves every feasible point satisfying \(f(x)<U-\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_U(X)=\varnothing\Longrightarrow\nexists x\in S\cap X\text{ with }f(x)<U-\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Validated contractor including the incumbent cutoff

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The empty-image pruning implication is logically sound and the certificate kind fits, but the record has no source. A specific authoritative locator for improving-point or cutoff contractors is required.

children.title: Propagation-Stagnation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Search regimes where contractor propagation yields little contraction before subdivision.

knowledge_statements.title: Propagation-Stagnation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-point propagation may fail to separate feasible and infeasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A contractor has stagnated on \(X\) when a complete propagation sweep returns \(C(X)=X\) while \(X\) remains nondegenerate. Stagnation certifies neither feasibility nor infeasibility and therefore cannot alone justify pruning. For the equality constraint \(x-y=0\) on \(X=[0,1]^2\), standard coordinate projections may return the entire box because each coordinate range is supported by some value of the other coordinate, although most points of \(X\) violate the equality. An unresolved stagnated box must be retained, strengthened with another relaxation, or subdivided.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contractor fixed point need not be feasible: dependency can prevent contraction, so unresolved stagnated boxes require stronger reasoning or subdivision.
assumptions_latex: The contractor is inclusion-valid and contracting.
No independent infeasibility or objective-dominance certificate has been obtained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C(X)=X\not\Longrightarrow X\subseteq S\), and \(C(X)=X\not\Longrightarrow X\cap S=\varnothing\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-point warning and equality example are plausible, but neither the contractor-stagnation claim nor the behavior of the stated coordinate projections has a cited source.

children.title: Interval Certificate Layer

knowledge_statements.title: Interval Certificate Layer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validated boxwise enclosures supporting infeasibility, dominance, and optimality-gap decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq X_0\) be the feasible set, and let \(\mathcal B\) be a validated box cover of every feasible point not previously removed by a sound certificate. For each \(X\in\mathcal B\), the interval certificate layer stores outward-rounded constraint enclosures and an objective enclosure \(F(X)=[L(X),R(X)]\) satisfying \(f(x)\in F(X)\) for every \(x\in S\cap X\). Given a validated feasible incumbent value \(U\), a box is dominance-prunable if \(L(X)\ge U-\varepsilon\), and it is infeasibility-prunable if a validated constraint enclosure or contractor proves \(X\cap S=\varnothing\). If every box in \(\mathcal B\) satisfies one of these pruning conditions, then the incumbent is globally \(\varepsilon\)-optimal. Each decision is checkable from the stored box, enclosures, and rounding convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outward-rounded interval bounds certify box infeasibility or inability to improve the feasible incumbent, and certificates covering every unresolved feasible point establish a global optimality gap.
assumptions_latex: All stored interval evaluations use inclusion-valid outward rounding.
\(U=f(\hat x)\) for a validated feasible point \(\hat x\in S\).
\(\mathcal B\) covers every feasible point not already removed by a sound certificate.
\(\varepsilon>0\), and the global minimum \(f^*=\min_{x\in S}f(x)\) exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigl(L(X)\ge U-\varepsilon\text{ or }X\cap S=\varnothing\bigr)\) for every \(X\in\mathcal B\) implies \(U-f^*\le\varepsilon\).

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Basic Concepts of Global Optimization p. 33

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty box, let \(m\in\mathbb{N}_0\), and let \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m:B\to\mathbb{R}\). Define \(F_B=\{x\in B:g_i(x)\le 0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\). A spatial relaxation consists of a tractable set \(R_B\supseteq F_B\) and a function \(\phi_B:R_B\to\mathbb{R}\) satisfying \(\phi_B(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in F_B\). Its value is \[L_{\mathrm{sp}}(B)=\inf_{z\in R_B}\phi_B(z).\] Consequently, \(L_{\mathrm{sp}}(B)\le\inf_{x\in F_B}f(x)\). Under the convention \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\), the layer may return \(+\infty\) only if it has certified \(F_B=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A spatial relaxation enlarges the feasible set and underestimates the objective on every original feasible point, thereby producing a certified lower bound for the box subproblem.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each active box \(B\), let \(F_B\) be its feasible set, let \(f:F_B\to\mathbb{R}\) be the objective, and define \(p(B)=\inf_{x\in F_B}f(x)\). Suppose the interval and spatial layers supply certified bounds \(L_{\mathrm{int}}(B)\le p(B)\) and \(L_{\mathrm{sp}}(B)\le p(B)\), and let \(U\in\mathbb{R}\) be the objective value of a validated feasible incumbent. The exchanged lower bound is \[L(B)=\max\{L_{\mathrm{int}}(B),L_{\mathrm{sp}}(B)\}.\] Then \(L(B)\le p(B)\). Hence \(B\) is safely discarded when \(L(B)>U\), or when \(L(B)\ge U-\varepsilon\) under a declared absolute \(\varepsilon\)-optimality convention with \(\varepsilon\ge0\). Any improved validated feasible value may decrease the shared incumbent \(U\), and any validated contraction of \(B\) may be supplied to both bounding layers before their bounds are recomputed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified interval and spatial-relaxation lower bounds combine by their maximum; validated feasible values update the shared upper bound used for safe pruning.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybridization Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of validation when an uncertified bound enters a pruning decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=[0,1]\), \(f(x)=(x-\tfrac12)^2\), and suppose a spatial solver reports the nonrigorous value \(\widetilde L_{\mathrm{sp}}(B)=10^{-2}\), although \(\inf_{x\in B}f(x)=0\). If this value is combined by \(\max\) with a certified interval lower bound and an incumbent \(U=5\times10^{-3}\), the rule \(\max\{L_{\mathrm{int}}(B),\widetilde L_{\mathrm{sp}}(B)\}>U\) discards \(B\), including its global minimizer. Thus a floating-point relaxation value may influence branching heuristics, but it cannot support validated pruning unless its lower-bound direction and numerical error are certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single uncertified relaxation bound can invalidate max-bound pruning and remove the true minimizer, even when the interval bound is rigorous.
assumptions_latex: Pruning uses the maximum of all reported lower bounds.
At least one reported bound lacks a rigorous lower-bound guarantee.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Validated global optimality is not preserved when an uncertified bound participates in pruning.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is mathematically coherent and the failure_boundary kind exactly fits the leaf: a reported value of 0.01 exceeds the true minimum 0 and can cause erroneous pruning against U=0.005. However, the record supplies neither a source nor an explicit standard-field rationale, so it does not satisfy the evidence contract.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_0=\prod_{i=1}^n[\underline x_i,\overline x_i]\subset\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(F_0\subseteq B_0\) be the feasible set, and consider minimizing \(f:F_0\to\mathbb{R}\). Given \(\varepsilon\ge0\), a certified operator satisfying \(L(B)\le\inf_{x\in F_0\cap B}f(x)\) for every processed box \(B\), and validated feasibility and feasible-value operators, initialize \(\mathcal A=\{B_0\}\) and \(U=+\infty\). Repeatedly select \(B\in\mathcal A\), apply validated contraction, update \(U\) from validated feasible points, and discard \(B\) if it is certified infeasible or, for finite \(U\), if \(L(B)\ge U-\varepsilon\). Otherwise bisect \(B\) into two children whose union is \(B\) and insert every unresolved child. If \(\mathcal A=\varnothing\) and \(U<+\infty\), then the incumbent is absolutely \(\varepsilon\)-globally optimal over \(F_0\). If \(\mathcal A=\varnothing\), \(U=+\infty\), and every discarded region was certified infeasible, then \(F_0=\varnothing\).

children.title: Regular Subpaving Search

knowledge_statements.title: Regular Subpaving Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary-tree representation of classified unions of regular boxes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a root box \(B_0\subset\mathbb R^n\) and a deterministic rule that bisects each splittable box into two axis-aligned children with disjoint interiors and union equal to the parent. A finite regular subpaving is the leaf set of a finite tree generated by repeated applications of this rule. If each leaf has a label in \(\{\mathrm{in},\mathrm{out},\mathrm{boundary},\mathrm{undecided}\}\), then the region represented by label \(q\) is \[S_q=\bigcup\{B:B\text{ is a leaf labelled }q\}.\] Search refines an undecided leaf by replacing it with its children and classifying each child using validated inclusion, exclusion, or boundary tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regular subpaving is a binary tree of boxes whose labeled leaves represent inner, outer, boundary, and unresolved portions of a region.
assumptions_latex: Every split produces two children covering the parent with disjoint interiors.
Leaf classifications are produced by validated predicates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The labeled leaf unions provide a refinement-stable region representation within \(B_0\).

notation.meaning: Union of leaves carrying classification q.

knowledge_statements.title: Priority-Queue Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Best-key-first implementation of validated box search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a root box \(B_0\) and a totally ordered key \(k(B)\), initialize a priority queue \(Q\) with \(B_0\). At each iteration extract a box \(B\) having minimal key, apply validated contraction, bounding, incumbent update, and pruning, and, if unresolved, partition \(B\) into covering children. Compute each child's key only from currently available search data and insert every unpruned child into \(Q\). Ties are resolved by a fixed rule. The algorithm stops with a global certificate only when \(Q\) is empty; queue ordering affects exploration order and efficiency, but not pruning validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Priority-queue search always processes an active box with best key, while validated tests alone determine pruning and certification.
assumptions_latex: The queue returns a minimal-key active box.
Pruning decisions use certified bounds rather than queue keys alone.
Every unresolved child is inserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The key changes search order but preserves certified exhaustion when all pruning tests are valid.

notation.meaning: Ordering key assigned to box B.

children.title: Queue-Key Semantics
children.top_down_role: Lower-bound, width, depth, uncertainty, and incumbent-sensitive priority keys.

knowledge_statements.title: Queue-Key Semantics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions separating priority semantics from certified pruning semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A queue key is a map \(k:\mathcal A\to\mathbb K\) into a totally ordered set. For best-lower-bound search one sets \(k(B)=L(B)\); for largest-first search one may set \(k(B)=-\operatorname{diam}(B)\); lexicographic combinations are also admissible. A key is certificate-safe precisely when either it is used only for ordering, or every pruning inference made from it follows from certified quantities encoded by the key. In particular, the implication \[k(B)\ge U-\varepsilon\Longrightarrow \inf_{x\in F_B}f(x)\ge U-\varepsilon\] must hold before a key comparison may discard \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Queue keys may rank boxes arbitrarily, but a key can justify pruning only when its comparison implies a certified objective bound.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb K\) is totally ordered.
\(U\) is a validated incumbent and \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Ordering-only keys preserve correctness; pruning keys additionally require the displayed certified implication.

notation.meaning: Certified lower bound for box B.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits queue-key semantics, and the displayed implication correctly states what is needed when a key comparison itself triggers pruning. No citation or explicit standard-field rationale is supplied, however, so the record lacks required evidence.

children.title: Search-State Memory Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Memory growth and stale-entry issues in large unresolved-region collections.

knowledge_statements.title: Search-State Memory Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Memory requirements for active-list and depth-first box search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose each stored box in \(\mathbb R^n\), together with its bound and fixed-size metadata, requires \(\Theta(n)\) words. If a best-first active set reaches \(N\) boxes, its search-state memory is \(\Theta(Nn)\) words, excluding shared model data and solver workspaces. For binary depth-first traversal of maximum depth \(d\), retaining only the current path and at most one pending sibling per level requires \(O(dn)\) words. These bounds cease to apply when node-local relaxations, contractors, or derivative enclosures have superlinear representation size; their storage must then be added per retained node.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Best-first search stores all active boxes, whereas depth-first traversal can store only a path and pending siblings; node-local solver objects add separate costs.
assumptions_latex: A box and fixed metadata occupy \(\Theta(n)\) words.
Subdivision is binary.
Shared model and solver-workspace memory is excluded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Best-first state uses \(\Theta(Nn)\) words, while depth-first state uses \(O(dn)\) words under the stated storage model.

notation.meaning: Maximum number of simultaneously active boxes.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity_bound kind exactly fits the memory-boundary leaf, and the asymptotic claims are coherent under the stated storage model. The record nevertheless has no source or explicit standard-field rationale for the memory bounds.

children.title: Widest-Coordinate Bisection
children.top_down_role: Subdivision driven by normalized or absolute box width.

assumptions_latex: \(B\) is a nonempty bounded axis-aligned box with positive width in at least one coordinate.
Every scale \(s_i\) is strictly positive.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(B=\prod_{i=1}^n[\underline x_i,\overline x_i]\), define \(w_i=\overline x_i-\underline x_i\), assume \(\max_i w_i>0\), and fix scales \(s_i>0\). Choose \(j\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{1\le i\le n} w_i/s_i\); absolute widest-coordinate bisection uses \(s_i=1\). With \(m_j=(\underline x_j+\overline x_j)/2\), form \(B^-\) and \(B^+\) by replacing the \(j\)-th interval respectively by \([\underline x_j,m_j]\) and \([m_j,\overline x_j]\). Then the children cover \(B\), have disjoint interiors, and each has selected-coordinate width \(w_j/2>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select a coordinate of greatest scaled positive width and split its interval at the midpoint, producing two covering child boxes with disjoint interiors.

children.title: Sensitivity-Scored Subdivision
children.top_down_role: Subdivision driven by coordinate width and certified sensitivity information.

children.title: Smear-Based Subdivision
children.top_down_role: Coordinate selection using width-weighted derivative or influence information.

knowledge_statements.title: Smear-Based Subdivision
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint smear score combining interval derivatives and box widths.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=\prod_{j=1}^n X_j\) and let \(g_i(x)=0\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), be constraints with interval derivative enclosures \(D_{ij}(B)\supseteq\{\partial g_i/\partial x_j(x):x\in B\}\). Define \(M_{ij}=\sup\{|d|:d\in D_{ij}(B)\}\) and the coordinate smear score \[S_j=\operatorname{wid}(X_j)\max_{1\le i\le m}M_{ij}.\] Select any \(j\in\operatorname*{argmax}_k S_k\) and bisect \(X_j\), normally at its midpoint. If all scores vanish or are unavailable, invoke a declared geometric fallback such as widest-coordinate bisection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Smear subdivision bisects the coordinate having the largest product of interval width and maximal enclosed constraint derivative magnitude.
assumptions_latex: Each \(g_i\) is differentiable on the box.
Every \(D_{ij}(B)\) rigorously encloses the corresponding derivative range.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected coordinate maximizes the declared smear score \(S_j\).

notation.meaning: Interval enclosure of a constraint partial derivative.
Maximum absolute magnitude in the derivative enclosure.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind is appropriate, but multiple smear heuristics exist, including different aggregations across constraints and derivative normalizations. With no cited source, the particular maximum-based score and fallback convention cannot be confirmed as the intended variant.

children.title: Sensitivity-Based Subdivision
children.top_down_role: Coordinate selection using certified objective or constraint sensitivity.

knowledge_statements.title: Sensitivity-Based Subdivision
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic rigorous sensitivity-score subdivision for objective reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=\prod_{j=1}^n X_j\) and suppose \(D_j(B)\) rigorously encloses \(\{\partial f/\partial x_j(x):x\in B\}\). Define \[S_j=\operatorname{wid}(X_j)\sup\{|d|:d\in D_j(B)\}.\] Choose any \(j\in\operatorname*{argmax}_k S_k\) and bisect \(X_j\) at a point strictly between its endpoints, using the midpoint unless another validated split rule is declared. The score estimates the coordinate's first-order contribution to objective-range overestimation. If every score is zero, nonfinite, or unavailable, apply a geometry-based fallback to ensure subdivision continues.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sensitivity subdivision splits the coordinate whose width times enclosed objective-derivative magnitude is largest, with a geometric fallback for unusable scores.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable on \(B\).
Each \(D_j(B)\) rigorously encloses the derivative range.
The selected split point lies in the interior of \(X_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm bisects a coordinate maximizing the rigorous sensitivity score \(S_j\).

notation.meaning: Interval enclosure of the j-th objective derivative.
The j-th coordinate interval of B.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but the width-times-objective-derivative score is one possible sensitivity heuristic rather than a uniquely determined definition. A source is needed to support the selected variant and the claim that it estimates objective-range overestimation.

children.title: Coordinate-Score Regimes
children.top_down_role: Scoring choices for balancing coordinate width, influence, and uncertainty.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate-Score Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A normalized family interpolating between width-driven and derivative-sensitivity subdivision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a box \(X=\prod_{i=1}^n X_i\), positive scales \(d_i\), derivative enclosures \(D_i(X)\supseteq\{\partial_i f(x):x\in X\}\), and \(\delta>0\), define \(w_i=\operatorname{wid}(X_i)/d_i\), \(M_i=\sup\{|v|:v\in D_i(X)\}\), and \(s_i^{(\alpha)}=w_i^{\alpha}(M_i+\delta)^{1-\alpha}\). Subdivide a coordinate in \(\operatorname*{argmax}_i s_i^{(\alpha)}\). The regimes \(\alpha=1\), \(\alpha=0\), and \(0<\alpha<1\) are respectively width-only, sensitivity-only, and mixed scoring; ties require a fixed deterministic rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalized coordinate scores interpolate between widest-coordinate, sensitivity-only, and mixed subdivision, with the largest score determining the split coordinate.
assumptions_latex: X=\prod_{i=1}^n X_i\subset\mathbb R^n
d_i>0\text{ and }\delta>0
D_i(X)\text{ encloses }\partial_i f\text{ on }X
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: i_*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{1\le i\le n}s_i^{(\alpha)}

children.title: Sensitivity-Enclosure Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Subdivision degradation caused by broad, unstable, or misleading sensitivity enclosures.

knowledge_statements.title: Sensitivity-Enclosure Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependency-induced derivative overestimation can make sensitivity scores select an irrelevant coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[-1,1]^2\), \(0<\varepsilon<4\), and evaluate \(f(x_1,x_2)=x_1^2-x_1^2+\varepsilon x_2\) without algebraic cancellation. Natural interval differentiation gives \(D_1(X)=2X_1-2X_1=[-4,4]\) and \(D_2(X)=[\varepsilon,\varepsilon]\), although \(\partial_1f\equiv0\). With equal coordinate widths and scores \(s_i=\operatorname{wid}(X_i)\sup|D_i(X)|\), one obtains \(s_1=8>s_2=2\varepsilon\). Thus sensitivity subdivision chooses \(x_1\), which has no true influence on the objective; algebraic reformulation or sharper derivative enclosures can reverse the decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Overestimated derivative intervals may assign the largest score to a coordinate whose true derivative is zero, making subdivision representation-dependent.
assumptions_latex: 0<\varepsilon<4
s_i=\operatorname{wid}(X_i)\sup\{|v|:v\in D_i(X)\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s_1>s_2\quad\text{while}\quad\partial_1f\equiv0

notation.meaning: interval enclosure of the ith partial derivative

children.title: Constraint-Informed Subdivision

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Informed Subdivision
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subdivision prioritizes poorly contracted coordinates influential in unresolved constraint boundaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(X\), constraints \(g_j(x)\le0\), a sound contractor \(C(X)\subseteq X\), and interval derivatives \(G_{ji}(X)\), discard \(X\) if the contractor proves infeasibility. Otherwise set \(Y=C(X)\), \(J(Y)=\{j:0\in g_j(Y)\}\), \(r_i=\operatorname{wid}(Y_i)/\operatorname{wid}(X_i)\), and \(b_i=\max_{j\in J(Y)}\sup|G_{ji}(Y)|\). If \(J(Y)\ne\varnothing\), bisect an index maximizing \(r_i\operatorname{wid}(Y_i)b_i\); otherwise bisect a widest normalized coordinate. Return the two outward-rounded child boxes, stopping only when the prescribed width tolerance or a validated pruning test applies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Contract first, then split the coordinate that remains wide and strongly influences an unresolved constraint boundary; use widest-coordinate subdivision otherwise.

C\text{ is a sound constraint contractor}
G_{ji}(Y)\supseteq\{\partial_i g_j(y):y\in Y\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: i_*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_i r_i\operatorname{wid}(Y_i)b_i\quad\text{when }J(Y)\ne\varnothing

children.title: Interval-Newton-Informed Subdivision

knowledge_statements.title: Interval-Newton-Informed Subdivision
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual coordinate widths after a Newton image determine anisotropic subdivision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a box \(X\) and a sound interval-Newton image \(N(X)\), discard \(X\) when \(X\cap N(X)=\varnothing\). Otherwise set \(Y=X\cap N(X)\) and \(q_i=\operatorname{wid}(Y_i)/\operatorname{wid}(X_i)\). If \(Y\subsetneq X\), retain \(Y\) as the contracted region. Unless a validated stopping or pruning test applies, bisect an index maximizing \(q_i\operatorname{wid}(Y_i)\), using a widest-coordinate tie rule. The resulting children are processed with fresh Newton images; hence failed or weak coordinate contraction receives subdivision priority.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersect with the interval-Newton image, discard empty intersections, and split the coordinate retaining the greatest residual width after contraction.

N(X)\text{ is a sound interval-Newton image}
\operatorname{wid}(X_i)>0\text{ for splittable coordinates}

children.title: Region-Selection Calculus
children.top_down_role: Traversal policies governing bound improvement, memory, and refinement fairness.

children.title: Best-Lower-Bound Selection
children.top_down_role: Priority given to regions with the smallest certified lower bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Best-Lower-Bound Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Best-first selection for a minimization branch-and-bound search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a finite active family \(\mathcal A\) of boxes and certified objective lower bounds \(L(B)\le\inf_{x\in B}f(x)\). At each iteration with \(\mathcal A\ne\varnothing\), remove a box \(B_*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal A}L(B)\), using a fixed tie rule, then contract, prune, or subdivide it. Insert every unpruned child with its certified lower bound. With incumbent value \(U\) and tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), prune only boxes satisfying \(L(B)\ge U-\varepsilon\). Stop when \(\mathcal A=\varnothing\) or, for nonempty \(\mathcal A\), when \(U-\min_{B\in\mathcal A}L(B)\le\varepsilon\), and return the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Always process the active box with the smallest certified lower bound, pruning only boxes unable to improve the incumbent beyond tolerance and stopping when the certified global gap is within tolerance.
assumptions_latex: L(B)\le\inf_{x\in B}f(x)\text{ for every active box }B
U\text{ is the value of a feasible incumbent}
\varepsilon\ge0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B_*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal A}L(B)

children.title: Depth-First Interval Search

knowledge_statements.title: Depth-First Interval Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LIFO traversal refines one surviving branch before returning to deferred siblings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a last-in-first-out stack \(S=[X_0]\). While \(S\ne\varnothing\), pop its top box \(B\), compute validated bounds and contractions, and discard \(B\) only by a certified infeasibility, dominance, or tolerance test. If \(B\) remains unresolved, bisect it into \(B^-\) and \(B^+\), push one child and then the preferred child last so that the preferred child is processed next. Update the incumbent only with feasible points. Terminate when the stack is empty or a separately validated global-gap criterion holds, and return the incumbent and its certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A LIFO stack repeatedly refines the newest surviving child, deferring siblings while retaining validated pruning and global termination tests.

all pruning tests are sound
every unresolved nonterminal box is subdivided

children.title: Breadth-First Region Selection

knowledge_statements.title: Breadth-First Region Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: FIFO traversal processes generated boxes in nondecreasing subdivision depth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a first-in-first-out queue \(Q=[(X_0,0)]\). Repeatedly remove the head \((B,d)\), apply validated contraction, bounding, and pruning, and, if \(B\) remains unresolved, subdivide it into finitely many children \(B_1,\ldots,B_m\). Append \((B_1,d+1),\ldots,(B_m,d+1)\) to the tail in a fixed order. Update the incumbent only from feasible points. Stop when \(Q\) is empty or a validated global-gap condition holds. In the absence of pruning, boxes are selected in nondecreasing depth.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A FIFO queue processes all earlier-generated regions before later descendants, yielding nondecreasing-depth traversal when regions are not pruned.

each subdivision produces finitely many children
all pruning tests are sound

children.title: Fair Region Scheduling
children.top_down_role: Scheduling regimes that prevent persistent neglect of unresolved regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Fair Region Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A scheduler is fair when no continuously eligible region can wait forever.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A_k\) be the active regions immediately before selection \(k\). A region scheduler is fair if, for every region \(B\) and every index \(k_0\) with \(B\in\mathcal A_{k_0}\), there exists a finite \(k\ge k_0\) such that either \(B\) is selected at iteration \(k\), or before iteration \(k\) it is removed by a sound pruning or contraction-replacement operation. Equivalently, a region that remains continuously active and eligible cannot be bypassed at every subsequent selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fairness requires every region that stays active to be selected after finitely many steps unless a sound operation removes or replaces it first.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal A_k\text{ is finite at every iteration }k
selected regions are drawn from \mathcal A_k
removal without selection uses a sound validated operation
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B\in\mathcal A_{k_0}\Longrightarrow\exists k\ge k_0:\ B\text{ is selected or soundly removed by }k

children.title: Coverage Guarantees
children.top_down_role: Exhaustive regional coverage supported by systematic traversal.

knowledge_statements.title: Coverage Guarantees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fair exhaustive subdivision eventually resolves every nonpruned point at arbitrary spatial scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(X_0\) is compact, subdivision is exhaustive in the sense that every infinite nested child chain \(B_0\supset B_1\supset\cdots\) satisfies \(\operatorname{diam}(B_k)\to0\), and region scheduling is fair. If \(x\in X_0\) is never excluded by a sound pruning operation, then for every \(\eta>0\) the search eventually selects or generates a box \(B\ni x\) with \(\operatorname{diam}(B)\le\eta\). Thus no persistent feasible neighborhood can remain forever unresolved solely because of scheduling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fair scheduling plus exhaustive subdivision eventually covers every nonpruned point with boxes of arbitrarily small diameter.

every infinite nested child chain has diameter tending to zero
the region scheduler is fair

children.title: Starvation Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions under which priority bias compromises fair exploration.

knowledge_statements.title: Starvation Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unfair priority selection may leave an eligible region permanently unprocessed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the initial active family be \(\mathcal A_0=\{A,B_0\}\), assign priorities \(p(A)=1\) and \(p(B_k)=0\), and always select a minimum-priority region. Suppose processing \(B_k\) removes it and creates the single active child \(B_{k+1}\), while no validated test removes \(A\). Then iteration \(k\) selects \(B_k\), after which \(\mathcal A_{k+1}=\{A,B_{k+1}\}\). Consequently \(A\) remains active but is never selected. Any convergence claim requiring eventual refinement of every persistent region therefore fails without fairness, aging, or periodic coverage selections.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strict priority rule can process an endless descendant chain while one eligible region remains active forever, invalidating coverage guarantees.

p(A)=1\text{ and }p(B_k)=0\text{ for every }k

children.title: Hybrid Search Scheduling
children.top_down_role: Mixed traversal policies combining multiple region-selection priorities.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Search Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Periodic fair selections are interleaved with aggressive bound- or depth-based refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain an active family \(\mathcal A\), a FIFO queue of creation order, certified lower bounds, and an incumbent \(U\). Fix an integer \(q\ge2\). At iterations divisible by \(q\), select the oldest still-active region; at every other iteration, select an active region maximizing a prescribed exploitation priority, such as bound improvement potential. Remove stale queue entries, apply only validated pruning, subdivide unresolved selections, and enqueue all surviving children. Stop on emptiness or a validated global-gap condition. Because at least every \(q\)-th selection is FIFO, each persistent region is eventually selected despite intervening aggressive refinements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interleave aggressive region priorities with periodic FIFO selections, preserving exploitation while preventing persistent regions from starving.

each iteration creates finitely many active children
all pruning and stopping tests are validated

children.title: Incumbent-Driven Region Selection
children.top_down_role: Search priorities shaped by certified feasible objective values.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent-Driven Region Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection uses certified potential improvement relative to the current feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization, maintain a feasible incumbent value \(U\), active boxes \(\mathcal A\), certified lower bounds \(L(B)\), and positive effort estimates \(c(B)\). Remove every box satisfying \(L(B)\ge U-\varepsilon\). For each remaining box define \(P_U(B)=(U-L(B))/c(B)\), and select \(B_*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal A}P_U(B)\), with a fixed tie rule. After contraction or subdivision, recompute bounds and priorities; whenever a better feasible point is found, decrease \(U\) and reprioritize all active boxes. Stop only under a validated emptiness or global-gap test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select the active box offering the greatest certified improvement below the incumbent per estimated effort, and reprioritize whenever the incumbent improves.
assumptions_latex: L(B)\le\inf_{x\in B}f(x)\text{ for every }B\in\mathcal A
U\text{ is the value of a feasible point}
c(B)>0\text{ and }\varepsilon\ge0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B_*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal A}\frac{U-L(B)}{c(B)}

notation.meaning: certified lower bound on region B

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The effort-normalized priority is bespoke and unsupported by the locator. Moreover, \(U-L(B)\) bounds possible improvement; it does not certify that such improvement is attainable, so the plain-language characterization is overstated.

children.title: Policy Switching Regimes
children.top_down_role: Conditions governing transitions among traversal priorities.

assumptions_latex: The active list \(\mathcal L_k\) is finite, and every retained box has a rigorous lower bound \(L(B)\) and width \(w(B)\).
The incumbent value \(U_k\) is the objective value of a certified feasible point.
A fairness threshold \(q\in\mathbb N\) bounds how long any retained box may be denied selection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every box that remains eligible indefinitely is eventually selected, while incumbent-sensitive selection is used whenever the fairness threshold is inactive.

notation.meaning: Validated lower bound and incumbent upper bound

review_flags: authoritative source for this precise switching rule is missing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A fair switch between best-bound traversal and progress-enforcing traversal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize an age counter \(a_k(B)=0\) for each inserted box \(B\). At iteration \(k\), if some \(B\in\mathcal L_k\) satisfies \(a_k(B)\ge q\), select an eligible box of maximal age; otherwise select a minimizer of \(L(B)\), breaking ties by larger \(w(B)\). Process the selected box by validated contraction, pruning, or subdivision. Delete rejected boxes, assign age zero to new children, and increment the ages of all unselected retained boxes. Stop when \(\mathcal L_k=\varnothing\) or when \(U_k-\min_{B\in\mathcal L_k}L(B)\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Switch to an oldest-box rule when a box waits too long; otherwise use best-bound selection. This preserves incumbent-driven search while preventing permanent starvation.
knowledge_statements.title: Policy Switching Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The age-threshold switching rule and its fairness claim are mathematically plausible but architecture-specific and uncited. The plain statement also omits material details of the algorithm and stopping rule.

children.title: Progress–Memory Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Balance between lower-bound progress, feasible-point discovery, and active storage.

assumptions_latex: Each active box stores a validated lower bound and incurs at least constant memory.
Boxes are removed only by validated pruning or processing.
The subdivision tree may have unbounded width.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Best-bound retention can require memory proportional to the active frontier, whereas depth-first traversal uses memory proportional to tree depth but may delay processing the globally best lower bound.

notation.meaning: Number of active boxes and current tree depth
Validated lower bound of a box

review_flags: memory constants depend on the queue and box representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case storage versus lower-bound prioritization in interval branch-and-bound traversal.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), retaining every live box in a best-bound priority queue requires \(\Theta(N_k)\) box records, where \(N_k\) is the active-frontier size, and permits immediate selection of a box attaining \(\min_B L(B)\). A depth-first implementation retaining only unexplored siblings along the current branch requires \(O(d_k)\) box records, where \(d_k\) is the current subdivision depth, but it need not select a globally least-bound box before completing deeper work. Thus bounded-memory traversal generally sacrifices immediate best-bound progress unless discarded frontier information is recomputed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Best-bound search stores the active frontier and prioritizes the strongest global candidate. Depth-first search stores only a path and siblings, but can postpone better-bound regions.
knowledge_statements.title: Progress–Memory Tradeoffs

children.title: Constrained Interval Search Architecture
children.top_down_role: Search organization specific to equality and inequality constraints.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Constrained Optimization: Controlling the Feasible Domain; Trouble with Constraints; Basic Algorithm

children.title: Feasible-Domain Control
children.top_down_role: Contractor and range-based classification of constrained search regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Domain Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Range tests and inclusion-preserving contractors for constrained interval boxes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), \(E=\{1,\ldots,p\}\), and \(F=\{x\in B:g_i(x)\le 0\ (i\in I),\ h_j(x)=0\ (j\in E)\}\). For a box \(B\), set \(B'=C(B)\). Reject \(B\) if \(B'=\varnothing\), if \(\inf G_i(B')>0\) for some \(i\in I\), or if \(0\notin H_j(B')\) for some \(j\in E\). If \(E=\varnothing\) and \(\sup G_i(B')\le 0\) for every \(i\in I\), classify \(B'\) as inner feasible. Otherwise classify \(B'\) as unresolved and retain it for further contraction or subdivision. The inclusion condition \(F\cap B\subseteq C(B)\subseteq B\) ensures that none of these rejection tests removes a feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Define the feasible set and constraint indices, contract each box, reject it only through rigorous range exclusion, certify wholly feasible inequality-only boxes, and retain all unresolved equality or boundary boxes.
assumptions_latex: The search box is \(B\subset\mathbb R^n\), with inequalities \(g_i(x)\le0\) for \(i\in I\) and equalities \(h_j(x)=0\) for \(j\in E\).
Each \(G_i(B)\) and \(H_j(B)\) encloses the range of its corresponding constraint on \(B\).
The contractor \(C\) satisfies \(F\cap B\subseteq C(B)\subseteq B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No feasible point is discarded; an inner box satisfies every inequality throughout the box, and every box not conclusively classified is retained for further processing.

notation.meaning: Feasible set in the current search box
Inequality and equality constraint index sets
