source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

children.title: Active-Face Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Search decomposition induced by active bounds and active nonlinear constraints.

children.title: Active Bound Sets
children.top_down_role: Search geometry induced by variables fixed at domain bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Active Bound Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-bound activity for boxes relative to an ambient search box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty box \(B\subseteq X\), define \[A^-(B)=\{i:\sup B_i\le \ell_i+\tau_i\},\qquad A^+(B)=\{i:\inf B_i\ge u_i-\tau_i\}.\] The active-bound signature is \(\mathcal A_b(B)=(A^-(B),A^+(B))\). When \(\tau_i=0\), membership means that the entire coordinate interval \(B_i\) is fixed at the corresponding bound. When \(\tau_i>0\), membership means that \(B_i\) is contained in the corresponding boundary slab. The tolerance restriction ensures \(A^-(B)\cap A^+(B)=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The signature records coordinates fixed at a domain bound when tolerance is zero and coordinates wholly contained in a lower or upper boundary slab when tolerance is positive.
assumptions_latex: The ambient box is \(X=[\ell,u]\subset\mathbb R^n\), with \(\ell_i<u_i\) for every \(i\).
The tolerances satisfy \(0\le\tau_i<(u_i-\ell_i)/2\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pair \((A^-(B),A^+(B))\) is an unambiguous exact-bound signature at zero tolerance and an unambiguous boundary-slab signature at positive tolerance.

source_refs.locator: 1.6.2 Face and Extreme Point p. 21

review_flags: positive-tolerance rule is an explicit algorithmic convention

source_witnesses.locator: 1.6.2 Face and Extreme Point p. 21

children.title: Active Nonlinear Constraint Sets
children.top_down_role: Regional structure associated with potentially binding nonlinear constraints.

assumptions_latex: The feasible region includes continuously differentiable inequalities \(g_i(x)\le0\).
A box \(B\) and nonnegative activity tolerances \(\eta_i\) are given.
Each interval evaluation \(G_i(B)\) encloses \(g_i(B)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting sets distinguish constraints whose zero level may meet the box from constraints certified strictly inactive throughout the box.

notation.meaning: Interval enclosure of the ith constraint over B

review_flags: precise activity convention varies across interval algorithms
authoritative source for this boxwise definition is missing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boxwise possible activity based on validated constraint ranges.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the possibly active nonlinear constraint set and the certified inactive set by \[A_g(B)=\{i:\inf G_i(B)\le0\le\sup G_i(B)+\eta_i\},\qquad I_g(B)=\{i:\sup G_i(B)<-\eta_i\}.\] A constraint with \(\inf G_i(B)>0\) instead certifies infeasibility of \(B\). Constraints not belonging to these three classes remain range-indeterminate because interval overestimation may straddle the activity thresholds. For \(\eta_i=0\), possible activity means that the validated range contains zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonlinear inequality is possibly active when its validated range reaches zero, strictly inactive when its upper range is negative, and infeasible when its lower range is positive.
knowledge_statements.title: Active Nonlinear Constraint Sets

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positive-tolerance activity convention is uncited and algorithm-dependent. Moreover, the plain statement says the range reaches zero, whereas the formula also treats ranges ending within eta below zero as possibly active.

children.title: Face-Based Search Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Organization of constrained search across lower-dimensional domain faces.

knowledge_statements.title: Face-Based Search Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact decomposition of a full-dimensional box into relative interiors of coordinate faces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For disjoint sets \(I,J\subseteq\{1,ldots,n\}\), let \(F_{I,J}^{\circ}\) be the set of points \(x\in X\) satisfying \(x_i=\ell_i\) for \(i\in I\), \(x_i=u_i\) for \(i\in J\), and \(\ell_i<x_i<u_i\) for \(i\notin I\cup J\). Then \[X=\mathop{\dot\bigcup}_{\substack{I,J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\\ I\cap J=\varnothing}}F_{I,J}^{\circ}.\] Thus every point has a unique active-bound signature. A validated search may organize certified boxes by these signatures while retaining every box whose signature remains unresolved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full-dimensional box is the disjoint union of the relative interiors of its coordinate faces, giving every point a unique active-bound signature; unresolved search boxes must remain in the search.
assumptions_latex: The domain is \(X=[\ell,u]\subset\mathbb R^n\), with \(\ell_i<u_i\) for every \(i\).
Only disjoint lower- and upper-active index pairs \((I,J)\) are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relative interiors of the coordinate faces form a disjoint decomposition of \(X\), and every point of \(X\) has a unique active-bound signature.

notation.meaning: Relative interior of the face indexed by lower- and upper-active sets

source_refs.locator: 1.6.2 Face and Extreme Point p. 21

source_witnesses.locator: 1.6.2 Face and Extreme Point p. 21

children.title: Active-Face Transition Regimes
children.top_down_role: Changes in relevant active sets across neighboring search regions.

assumptions_latex: A parent box is bisected into children whose union equals the parent.
Activity is classified by validated bound and nonlinear-constraint range tests.
Unresolved classifications are retained rather than discarded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A child is assigned a new face regime only after validated tests certify its signature; otherwise it remains in an unresolved transition regime.

notation.meaning: Combined bound and nonlinear activity signature
Parent box and one of its children

review_flags: authoritative source for the precise regime predicate is missing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certified changes of boxwise activity signatures under contraction or subdivision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Sigma(B)=(A^-(B),A^+(B),A_g(B))\). A child \(B'\subseteq B\) enters a certified transition regime when \(\Sigma(B')\ne\Sigma(B)\) and every changed membership is justified by a validated range inequality. It enters a stable regime when \(\Sigma(B')=\Sigma(B)\) and the relevant activity inequalities hold with strict margins. If any range overlaps an activity threshold, label the child unresolved. A transition rule is coverage-preserving only if unresolved children are contracted further or subdivided, never pruned solely because their signatures differ from the parent's.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After subdivision, change a box's active-face label only when validated tests certify the change. Any threshold-overlapping child remains unresolved and must stay in the search.
knowledge_statements.title: Active-Face Transition Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The transition predicate, strict-margin condition, and unresolved-state semantics are architecture-specific and have no cited support. Their precise mathematical version cannot be validated from the record.

children.title: Validated Feasible-Point Search
children.top_down_role: Certified feasible-point discovery for incumbent construction and equality-constrained verification.

knowledge_statements.title: Validated Feasible-Point Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certified incumbent construction, including existence verification for equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Generate a numerical candidate \(\hat x\in B\) and form a small box \(Y\subseteq B\) containing \(\hat x\). Apply the inclusion-preserving equality contractor \(C_h\). Reject the candidate if the contracted box is empty or if \(\inf G_i(Y)>0\) for some \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\). When equalities are present, return \(Y\) only if a valid interval Newton, Krawczyk, or other validated existence test certifies a point \(x^*\in Y\) satisfying \(h(x^*)=0\). In every case require \(\sup G_i(Y)\le0\) for all \(i\). A successful return supplies the incumbent value \(U=\sup [f](Y)\). Without equalities, a degenerate enclosure \(Y=[\hat x,\hat x]\) may be accepted after directed-rounding verification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enclose a numerical candidate, verify every inequality throughout its enclosure, and use a valid interval existence test when equalities are present. Success gives a certified feasible incumbent; failure remains inconclusive.
assumptions_latex: The problem has inequalities \(g_i(x)\le0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\), an equality map \(h:B\to\mathbb R^p\), and an objective \(f:B\to\mathbb R\).
The interval evaluations \(G_i\) and \([f]\) are inclusion-enclosing, and \(C_h\) is inclusion-preserving for the zero set of \(h\).
A returned equality enclosure is accepted only after a validated existence test, and all computations use outward rounding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every returned enclosure contains a feasible point and yields a rigorous incumbent upper bound; failure to return an enclosure does not certify infeasibility.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

review_flags: existence test must match the equality-system structure

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

children.title: Constraint-Boundary Refinement
children.top_down_role: Focused refinement of boxes unresolved near feasible-set boundaries.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Boundary Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive subdivision of boxes whose validated constraint ranges straddle feasibility boundaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an unresolved box \(B\), let \(J(B)\) be the finite set of constraints whose validated ranges contain the boundary value zero. Apply all available inclusion-preserving contractors. If the result remains unresolved, normally choose a coordinate \(r\) maximizing \(w_r(B)\max_{i\in J(B)}\sup|D_{ir}(B)|\). Use a widest-coordinate choice when the score vanishes and periodically whenever required by the fair-splitting safeguard. Bisect \(B\) in coordinate \(r\) and classify both children by validated range tests. Stop a branch only after validated rejection, inner-feasibility certification, objective pruning, or attainment of the prescribed width tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Contract boundary-ambiguous boxes, split a coordinate that strongly influences an ambiguous constraint, and periodically use widest-coordinate splitting to preserve fair refinement. Reclassify both children and retain every unresolved child above the requested resolution.
assumptions_latex: A box is unresolved because at least one validated constraint range contains its boundary value zero.
All pruning and contraction operations are inclusion-preserving.
The splitting safeguard selects a widest coordinate sufficiently often on every indefinitely refined branch.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The refinement does not discard feasible points. At fixed tolerance it localizes every unpruned boundary branch to the prescribed resolution; if refinement is continued with tolerances tending to zero, the fair-splitting safeguard makes persistent box diameters tend to zero. A box containing an actual constraint boundary may remain unresolved.

notation.meaning: Width of box B in coordinate r
Validated interval enclosure of the relevant partial derivative

review_flags: coordinate score is an admissible implementation choice

children.title: Contractor-Newton Contraction Pipeline
children.top_down_role: Aggressive domain contraction before or between subdivisions.

children.title: Contractor-Based Acceleration
children.top_down_role: Domain reduction through validated constraint or objective contractors.

knowledge_statements.title: Contractor-Based Acceleration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completeness-preserving box reduction before bounding and subdivision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a processed box \(B\), set \(B'=C(B)\). If \(S\cap B\subseteq C(B)\subseteq B\), then every target point represented by \(B\) remains represented by \(B'\), and \(B'=\varnothing\) certifies \(S\cap B=\varnothing\). Every coordinate width of \(B'\) is no greater than the corresponding width of \(B\). For an inclusion-isotonic objective extension \([f]\), one has \([f](B')\subseteq[f](B)\), so recomputed objective bounds are no weaker. The contracted box may therefore replace \(B\) before pruning or subdivision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inclusion-preserving contractor shrinks a box without losing target points. Recomputed inclusion-isotonic objective ranges and coordinate widths cannot become wider.
assumptions_latex: The contractor \(C\) satisfies \(S\cap B\subseteq C(B)\subseteq B\) for the target set \(S\).
The interval objective extension \([f]\) is inclusion-isotonic and is recomputed with outward rounding after contraction.
Subdivision remains exhaustive for boxes not eliminated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing a processed box by its contracted image preserves completeness and cannot increase any coordinate width or the inclusion-isotonic objective range.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

children.title: Interval Newton Acceleration
children.top_down_role: Newton-type validated contraction within global-search regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Interval Newton Acceleration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical interval Newton exclusion and strict-inclusion certificates for regular square systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal J=[J_h](B)\) and let \(N(x_0,B)\) be an outward-rounded interval enclosure of \(\{x_0-A^{-1}h(x_0):A\in\mathcal J\}\). Every zero of \(h\) in \(B\) belongs to \(N(x_0,B)\cap B\). Therefore \(N(x_0,B)\cap B=\varnothing\) certifies that \(B\) contains no zero. If \(N(x_0,B)\subset\operatorname{int}B\), the regular interval Newton theorem certifies exactly one zero in \(B\). In all other cases, \(N(x_0,B)\cap B\) may replace \(B\) whenever it is a proper subset.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a regular square-system interval Jacobian, the interval Newton image encloses every zero in the box. Empty intersection excludes zeros, while strict interior inclusion certifies a unique zero and supports contraction.
assumptions_latex: The map \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) is continuously differentiable on the box \(B\).
A point \(x_0\in B\) and an interval Jacobian enclosure \(\mathcal J=[J_h](B)\) are available.
Every matrix \(A\in\mathcal J\) is nonsingular, and the interval Newton image is computed with outward rounding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Disjointness excludes zeros; strict interior inclusion certifies a unique zero in \(B\); and intersection with the Newton image is inclusion-preserving.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

children.title: Composed Contraction Pipelines
children.top_down_role: Coordinated use of multiple contraction mechanisms between subdivisions.

assumptions_latex: Each stage \(C_r\) is inclusion-preserving for the same target set \(S\).
Every stage maps boxes to subsets of its input box.
Stopping tolerances are nonnegative and all interval operations use outward rounding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The composed pipeline is itself inclusion-preserving; iteration terminates under a finite stage cap and returns a box no larger than its input.
review_flags: pipeline ordering and stopping thresholds are implementation choices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential composition and controlled repetition of validated box contractors.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(B^{(0)}=B\), perform a sweep by setting \(B^{(r)}=C_r(B^{(r-1)})\) for \(r=1,\ldots,m\). Stop immediately if any \(B^{(r)}=\varnothing\). Otherwise let \(P(B)=B^{(m)}\), repeat sweeps while \(\Delta(B,P(B))=\max_i\bigl(w_i(B)-w_i(P(B))\bigr)>\delta\), and stop after at most \(s_{\max}\) sweeps. Return the final box. Since every stage preserves \(S\cap B\), their composition preserves it, and the returned boxes form a nested sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply validated contractors sequentially, repeat while contraction remains significant, and cap the number of sweeps. Composition preserves all target solutions and produces nested boxes.
knowledge_statements.title: Composed Contraction Pipelines

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

children.title: Acceleration Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Poor contraction regimes caused by singularity, dependency, or weak local structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Acceleration Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for validated contractor and interval-Newton acceleration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be a search box and let \(N(X)\) be an interval-Newton image or contractor output computed from valid outward-rounded enclosures. If the required linear enclosure cannot be validated, the interval system cannot be solved soundly, or no solution-preserving contraction is obtained, the acceleration step is inconclusive and \(X\) must be retained or subdivided. A verified solution-preserving output may replace \(X\) by \(X\cap N(X)\), and an empty intersection may justify deletion. Existence or uniqueness may be asserted only when the hypotheses and inclusion test of the particular interval-Newton or contractor theorem are satisfied; strict contraction alone is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Failure to construct a valid Newton enclosure or solution-preserving contraction makes acceleration inconclusive. Deletion, existence, and uniqueness require their respective validated exclusion or inclusion tests.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is a search box for a specified residual or constraint system.
Every interval and linear-system enclosure used by the acceleration step is computed with validated outward rounding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An inconclusive acceleration step cannot delete \(X\) or certify existence or uniqueness; those conclusions require the corresponding validated exclusion or inclusion test.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

children.title: Local-Search Acceleration
children.top_down_role: Incumbent improvement and candidate localization through conventional solvers.

assumptions_latex: \(f\) and all constraints are defined on a compact search box \(X_0\).
A conventional local solver may return an approximate point without validated guarantees.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only a separately certified feasible point may update the rigorous incumbent upper bound.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local optimization is used heuristically; validation remains separate.

source_refs.locator: 1.2.2 'Globalized' Local Optimization Strategies, Combined with Grid Search or Random Search p. 24

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a retained box \(X\), choose a start point \(x_0\in X\), run a local solver to obtain \(\hat x\), and use \(\hat x\) to prioritize or subdivide boxes. Before replacing the incumbent \(U\), validate that \(\hat x\in X_0\), that every equality and inequality constraint is satisfied under rigorous evaluation, and that an outward-rounded objective evaluation gives \(f(\hat x)\leq \widehat U<U\). If validation fails, retain \(U\); the unvalidated local result may guide search ordering but cannot justify pruning. Stop the local phase by its ordinary solver rule and return the validated incumbent and any candidate localization data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local solver proposes promising points and regions, but its result changes the rigorous incumbent or prunes boxes only after independent feasibility and objective validation.
knowledge_statements.title: Local-Search Acceleration

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2.2 'Globalized' Local Optimization Strategies, Combined with Grid Search or Random Search p. 24

children.title: Shape-Test Acceleration
children.top_down_role: Search reduction through monotonicity, convexity, and nonconvexity information.

assumptions_latex: \(f\in C^2(X)\) on a box \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\).
Derivative and Hessian enclosures are outward-rounded and contain all pointwise values on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Validated derivative signs, positive semidefinite curvature, or a uniform negative-curvature direction yield sound reductions or exclusions.

notation.meaning: interval enclosure of the partial derivative on the box
interval Hessian enclosure on the box

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validated monotonicity and curvature tests for box reduction.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(0\notin[\partial_i f](X)\), then \(f\) is strictly monotone in coordinate \(i\), so an unconstrained minimizer over \(X\) lies on the corresponding lower or upper face. If every point matrix in \([H_f](X)\) is positive semidefinite, then \(f\) is convex on \(X\), and validated first-order conditions are sufficient for global minimality within \(X\). If there exists \(d\neq0\) such that \(d^{\mathsf T}H d<0\) for every \(H\in[H_f](X)\), then no interior point of \(X\) is a local minimizer. Each reduction is permitted only when its sign or curvature predicate is rigorously certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rigorous derivative signs force minimizers to faces; certified convexity strengthens optimality tests; uniform negative curvature excludes interior local minimizers.
knowledge_statements.title: Shape-Test Acceleration

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

children.title: Incremental Interval Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Reuse of expression, derivative, and contractor information across related boxes.

assumptions_latex: A child box \(Y\) satisfies \(Y\subseteq X\).
Cached values are rigorous enclosures on the parent box \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reused information is sound only after restriction or intersection with a fresh enclosure valid on \(Y\).

notation.meaning: cached and newly evaluated interval enclosures

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound reuse of interval expression and contractor data across nested boxes.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a child box \(Y\subseteq X\), retrieve cached expression, derivative, or contractor data \(E_X\) known to enclose the relevant quantity on \(X\). Recompute every component whose validity depends on changed coordinate bounds, rounding context, or contractor state, obtaining \(E_Y^{\mathrm{new}}\). Set \(E_Y=E_X\cap E_Y^{\mathrm{new}}\) when both operands enclose the same quantity on \(Y\); otherwise use the operand whose validity on \(Y\) is certified. Apply cached contractor conclusions only after verifying their solution-preservation conditions for \(Y\). Output \(E_Y\) and updated cache metadata; never reuse a parent lower bound, derivative sign, or contraction outside its certified domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incremental evaluation reuses parent computations only on nested boxes and intersects them with valid child enclosures; domain-dependent or stale data must be recomputed.
knowledge_statements.title: Incremental Interval Evaluation

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

children.title: Validated Decision Soundness
children.top_down_role: Correctness families for containment, contraction, incumbent construction, and pruning.

children.title: Enclosure Soundness
children.top_down_role: Correctness of computed objective and constraint range containment.

assumptions_latex: \(h:D\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is defined on a box \(X\subseteq D\).
All elementary operations use directed outward rounding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h(X)\subseteq[\!h\!](X)\), componentwise.

notation.meaning: set-valued range of the point function over the box

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fundamental containment property for validated objective and constraint evaluation.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A computed interval extension \([\!h\!]\) is enclosure-sound on \(X\) when \[h(X)=\{h(x):x\in X\}\subseteq[\!h\!](X).\] For a scalar objective, writing \([\!f\!](X)=[L(X),U(X)]\) therefore implies \(L(X)\leq f(x)\leq U(X)\) for every \(x\in X\). For constraints, every component range must be contained componentwise. Consequently, exclusion based on a missing required value, or bounding based on an interval endpoint, is valid only when this containment property holds under the actual floating-point rounding mode and domain conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every computed objective or constraint interval must contain all exact values attained over its box; only then can its endpoints support validated decisions.
knowledge_statements.title: Enclosure Soundness

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

children.title: Contractor Soundness
children.top_down_role: Correctness of domain contraction relative to the target solution set.

knowledge_statements.title: Contractor Soundness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solution-preservation property for validated domain contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A contractor \(C\) is sound for the target set \(S\) on \(X_0\) if, for every box \(X\subseteq X_0\), \[C(X)\subseteq X\quad\text{and}\quad S\cap X=S\cap C(X).\] The first relation is contraction and the second is solution preservation. Thus \(C(X)=\varnothing\) certifies that \(S\cap X=\varnothing\), while a nonempty output permits replacement of \(X\) by \(C(X)\). A composition \(C_k\circ\cdots\circ C_1\) remains sound when every \(C_i\) is sound for the same target set on every intermediate domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sound contractor returns a subset of its input while preserving every target solution; an empty output therefore certifies that the input contains none.
assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq X_0\) is the target feasible or solution set.
\(C\) maps every box \(X\subseteq X_0\) to a box or box union contained in \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\cap X=S\cap C(X)\) ensures that contraction discards no target solution.

children.title: Incumbent Soundness
children.top_down_role: Correctness of certified feasible upper bounds.

assumptions_latex: The problem is \(f^*=\min\{f(x):x\in F\}\) with nonempty feasible set \(F\).
A candidate \(\hat x\) and its objective value are checked using rigorous enclosures.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Certified feasibility and \(f(\hat x)\leq U\) imply \(f^*\leq U\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible-point certificate for a rigorous global upper bound.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47
2.5 Local, Global, epsilon-Global Minima p. 57

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An incumbent value \(U\) is sound when there exists a certified point \(\hat x\in F\) such that a rigorous objective enclosure proves \(f(\hat x)\leq U\). Then \[f^*=\min_{x\in F}f(x)\leq f(\hat x)\leq U.\] For inequality constraints \(g_j(x)\leq0\) and equality constraints \(h_k(x)=0\), feasibility must be established by a point certificate appropriate to their representations; mere intersection of an interval constraint range with its admissible set is insufficient. An approximate local-solver point without such certification cannot update the rigorous incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rigorous upper bound requires a point whose feasibility is certified and whose outward-rounded objective value does not exceed the reported incumbent.
knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Soundness

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

children.title: Pruning Soundness
children.top_down_role: Correctness of objective, infeasibility, stationarity, and curvature rejection.

knowledge_statements.title: Pruning Soundness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validated rejection rules for boxes unable to contain a required improving feasible minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the feasible set. A retained box \(X\) may be pruned if a validated predicate proves at least one of the following: \(X\cap F=\varnothing\); \(L(X)>U\), or \(L(X)\geq U\) when ties need not be retained; or no point of \(X\cap F\) can be a local minimizer relative to \(F\), with all applicable boundary and constraint qualifications included in the test. Stationarity or curvature predicates must therefore be valid for the constrained problem, not merely for the unconstrained objective. Under these conditions, deleting \(X\) removes no feasible point with objective strictly below \(U\) and, under the chosen tie convention, no required global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pruning is sound only when validated infeasibility, objective bounds, or constraint-aware stationarity or curvature tests prove that the box contains no required improving feasible minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is the feasible set and \(L(X)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\cap F\).
\(U\) is a certified incumbent upper bound.
Any stationarity or curvature rejection test accounts for the constraints and relevant boundary points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A box may be removed only when a validated predicate proves that it contains no improving global minimizer required by the chosen tie convention.

notation.meaning: validated lower bound over feasible points in a box

children.title: Exhaustive-Refinement Convergence
children.top_down_role: Coverage-based convergence under persistent refinement of unresolved regions.

assumptions_latex: \(X_0\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is compact and every unresolved box is eventually processed.
Subdivision is exhaustive: along every infinite retained branch, box diameters tend to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every point never soundly excluded is covered at every stage by retained boxes of arbitrarily small diameter.

notation.meaning: retained box family after stage k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic convergence from fair processing and exhaustive subdivision.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.1 Convergence of Univariate Global Optimization Algorithms p. 75
3.6 Finite epsilon-Convergence and epsilon-Global Optimality p. 87

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z\in X_0\) be a point that satisfies the target conditions and is never removed by a sound pruning rule. If \(\mathcal B_k\) is the retained cover after stage \(k\), then for every \(k\) there exists \(X_k\in\mathcal B_k\) with \(z\in X_k\). Fair processing and exhaustive subdivision imply that one may choose such boxes along a nested retained branch satisfying \[\operatorname{diam}(X_k)\longrightarrow0.\] Hence every neighborhood of \(z\) eventually contains a retained descendant box covering \(z\). In particular, unresolved regions cannot remain indefinitely at positive diameter merely because other boxes are repeatedly selected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fair processing and persistent subdivision preserve coverage of every unexcluded target point while shrinking its retained boxes to arbitrarily small diameter.
knowledge_statements.title: Exhaustive-Refinement Convergence

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.1 Convergence of Univariate Global Optimization Algorithms p. 75

children.title: Consistent-Bound Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence through tightening regional bounds on shrinking domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Consistent-Bound Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence from uniformly consistent regional lower bounds and improving certified incumbents.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal B_k\) be a finite retained family covering a global minimizer, and define \(L_k=\min_{X\in\mathcal B_k}L(X)\). Suppose \(L(X)\leq\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\) for every retained box and \[\sup_{X\in\mathcal B_k}\left(\inf_{x\in X}f(x)-L(X)\right)\longrightarrow0.\] Then \(L_k\to f^*\). If certified incumbents satisfy \(U_k\geq f^*\) and \(U_k\to f^*\), then \[0\leq U_k-L_k\longrightarrow0.\] Consequently, termination with \(U_k-L_k\leq\varepsilon\) certifies \(\varepsilon\)-global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly consistent lower bounds over a retained cover converge to the global minimum; with convergent certified incumbents, the certified global optimality gap vanishes.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is continuous on a compact search domain, and each finite retained family \(\mathcal B_k\) covers at least one global minimizer.
Every \(L(X)\) is a sound lower bound, and the lower-bound error converges uniformly to zero over \(\mathcal B_k\).
The certified incumbents satisfy \(U_k\geq f^*\) and \(U_k\to f^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_k\to f^*\) and \(U_k-L_k\to0\).

notation.meaning: finite retained box family at stage k
minimum retained lower bound at stage k

children.title: Contractor-Compatible Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence when solution-preserving contraction is interleaved with exhaustive subdivision.

assumptions_latex: Every contractor is solution-preserving and returns a subset of its input.
Processing is fair, and every infinite retained branch is subdivided to vanishing diameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Interleaving sound contraction with subdivision preserves exhaustive convergence to every unpruned minimizer.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence preservation under sound contraction between subdivision steps.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47
3.6 Finite epsilon-Convergence and epsilon-Global Optimality p. 87

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) denote the global minimizer set. Suppose each contractor \(C_k\) satisfies \(M\cap X=M\cap C_k(X)\) on every processed box \(X\). Then replacing \(X\) by \(C_k(X)\), followed by exhaustive subdivision of every nonempty unresolved result, preserves coverage of \(M\). For each \(x^*\in M\) not deliberately omitted by the tie convention, there exists a retained sequence \(X_k\ni x^*\). If fairness and the subdivision rule ensure \(\operatorname{diam}(X_k)\to0\), contractor insertion cannot prevent convergence. A contractor that is merely contracting but not solution-preserving invalidates this conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sound contractors can be inserted between exhaustive subdivisions without losing minimizers or preventing retained boxes around them from shrinking to points.
knowledge_statements.title: Contractor-Compatible Convergence

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

children.title: Minimizer-Cover Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence of retained boxes toward the global minimizer set.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimizer-Cover Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hausdorff convergence of a finite retained minimizer cover.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty compact global minimizer set, let \(\mathcal B_k\) be a finite family of compact boxes, and set \(R_k=\bigcup_{X\in\mathcal B_k}X\). Assume \(M\subseteq R_k\), every \(X\in\mathcal B_k\) satisfies \(X\cap M\neq\varnothing\), and \(\delta_k=\max_{X\in\mathcal B_k}\operatorname{diam}(X)\to0\). Then \[d_H(R_k,M)\leq\delta_k\longrightarrow0.\] The condition that every retained box meets \(M\) is essential: minimizer coverage and shrinking individual boxes do not exclude persistent remote boxes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If finite retained box families cover the minimizer set, every retained box intersects that set, and their maximum diameter vanishes, then their unions converge to the minimizer set in Hausdorff distance.
assumptions_latex: The global minimizer set \(M\) is nonempty and compact.
Each \(\mathcal B_k\) is a finite family of compact boxes covering \(M\).
Every retained box meets \(M\), and the maximum retained-box diameter tends to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_H(R_k,M)\leq\delta_k\to0\).

notation.meaning: finite retained box family at stage k

children.title: Positive-Tolerance Finite Termination
children.top_down_role: Finite completion under prescribed value and region tolerances.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Tolerance Finite Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite certification for Lipschitz branch-and-bound under positive value and box-diameter tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^d\) be a compact box and let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) be \(L\)-Lipschitz. For every current box \(B\), let \(c_B\) be its center, \(r(B)=\sup_{x\in B}\lVert x-c_B\rVert\), and \(\ell(B)=f(c_B)-Lr(B)\). Suppose regular subdivision produces, after finitely many splits, boxes satisfying \(r(B)\le r\) and \(\operatorname{diam}(B)\le\varepsilon_x\). With \(U=\min_B f(c_B)\), if \(2Lr\le\varepsilon_f\), then \[U-\min_B\ell(B)\le 2Lr\le\varepsilon_f.\] Thus exhaustive validated search terminates finitely with both prescribed tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regular subdivision of a compact box finitely achieves any positive spatial tolerance, while Lipschitz center bounds then certify the prescribed objective-value gap.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subset\mathbb R^d\) is a compact box and \(f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz.
Subdivision is regular and exhaustive.
\(\varepsilon_f>0\) and \(\varepsilon_x>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U-\min_B\ell(B)\le\varepsilon_f\) and \(\max_B\operatorname{diam}(B)\le\varepsilon_x\) after finitely many subdivisions.

notation.meaning: validated lower bound on the minimum over box B
radius of B about its center

children.title: Exact Zero-Tolerance Finiteness
children.top_down_role: Special regimes permitting exact finite certification.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Zero-Tolerance Finiteness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An exact-arithmetic finite-partition regime in which zero-gap certification is possible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be the union of a known finite box partition \(\mathcal P=\{Q_1,\ldots,Q_m\}\). Suppose \(f\) is constant on each \(Q_i\), with value \(v_i\), and validated exact arithmetic returns the point enclosure \(F(Q_i)=[v_i,v_i]\). An exhaustive interval search that evaluates every member of \(\mathcal P\) terminates after at most \(m\) box evaluations. Its reported value \(v_* =\min_{1\le i\le m}v_i\) equals \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)\), and the union of boxes attaining \(v_*\) is the exact global solution region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact finite certification is possible when a known finite partition has exact constant-value enclosures and all partition cells are examined.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P\) is a finite partition of \(X\).
\(f\) is constant on every \(Q_i\in\mathcal P\).
All enclosure computations and comparisons are exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_*=\min_{x\in X}f(x)\) is certified with zero gap after at most \(m\) evaluations.

notation.meaning: known finite box partition of the search domain
validated range enclosure on partition box Q_i

children.title: Asymptotic Convergence Without Termination
children.top_down_role: Convergent searches unable to resolve exact distinctions finitely.

assumptions_latex: \(\alpha\in(-1,1)\setminus\mathbb Q\).
At stage \(k\), every interval in the level-\(k\) dyadic partition is evaluated and its endpoints and midpoint are sampled.
Interval ranges are evaluated exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U_k-L_k>0\) for every finite \(k\), while \(U_k-L_k\to0\) as \(k\to\infty\).

notation.meaning: best value among all sampled dyadic points through stage k
smallest exact interval lower bound at stage k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A complete levelwise dyadic interval search whose certified gap converges to zero but is never exactly zero.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(\alpha\in(-1,1)\setminus\mathbb Q\) and minimize \(f(x)=(x-\alpha)^2\) on \([-1,1]\). At stage \(k\), evaluate every interval in the level-\(k\) dyadic partition using exact interval range evaluation, and sample every partition endpoint and interval midpoint. Let \(U_k\) be the best sampled value and let \(L_k\) be the smallest interval lower bound. Every sampled point is dyadic and therefore differs from \(\alpha\), so \(U_k>0\). The unique dyadic interval containing \(\alpha\) has exact lower bound \(0\), so \(L_k=0\). Consequently, \(U_k-L_k>0\) at every finite stage. The dyadic mesh tends to zero and the sampled endpoints approach \(\alpha\), so \(U_k-L_k\to0\) as \(k\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complete dyadic search never samples an irrational minimizer at a finite stage, so its certified gap remains positive, although the increasingly fine dyadic samples make that gap converge to zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Asymptotic Convergence Without Termination

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

children.title: Precision-Limited Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Loss of progress when subdivision and contraction reach arithmetic resolution limits.

knowledge_statements.title: Precision-Limited Stagnation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subdivision failure at adjacent floating-point endpoints under outward-rounded interval arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a<b\) be adjacent numbers in a floating-point format, so no representable number lies strictly between them. For the interval \(B=[a,b]\), any representable rounded midpoint \(m=\operatorname{fl}((a+b)/2)\) equals \(a\) or \(b\). Consequently, the nominal children \([a,m]\) and \([m,b]\) include one child equal to \(B\). If an outward-rounded contractor also returns \(B\), repeated subdivision or contraction cannot reduce its representable width. Unless the algorithm detects this event or increases precision, a stopping test requiring a smaller positive width can fail indefinitely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adjacent floating-point endpoints admit no interior split, so an unchanged child can persist unless stagnation is detected or precision increases.
assumptions_latex: \(a<b\) are adjacent representable floating-point numbers.
Midpoints and interval operations use the fixed format.
The contractor maps \(B\) to \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{wid}(B)\) cannot be reduced representably by the stated subdivision-contraction step.

notation.meaning: rounding into the fixed floating-point format

children.title: Enclosure-Order Search-Rate Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Search behavior governed by the contraction order of enclosure excess.

children.title: Enclosure Excess Order
children.top_down_role: Asymptotic contraction quality of regional objective enclosures.

knowledge_statements.title: Enclosure Excess Order
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial order of lower-enclosure overestimation relative to box diameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), and let \(L(B)\le\inf_{x\in B}f(x)\) be a validated lower bound for each box \(B\subset X\). Define the enclosure excess by \(e(B)=\inf_{x\in B}f(x)-L(B)\ge0\). The lower-enclosure scheme has excess order at least \(p>0\) on \(X\) if constants \(C<\infty\) and \(h_0>0\) exist such that \[e(B)\le C\operatorname{diam}(B)^p\] for every admissible box \(B\subset X\) with \(\operatorname{diam}(B)\le h_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enclosure excess has order p when the gap between the true box minimum and its validated lower bound is bounded by a constant times diameter to p.
assumptions_latex: \(L(B)\le\inf_{x\in B}f(x)\) for every admissible box \(B\subset X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e(B)=O(\operatorname{diam}(B)^p)\) as \(\operatorname{diam}(B)\downarrow0\).

notation.meaning: validated lower bound on the minimum over B

children.title: Subdivision Search Rate
children.top_down_role: Reduction of unresolved search regions under repeated subdivision.

assumptions_latex: \(X=\prod_{i=1}^d[a_i,b_i]\subset\mathbb R^d\) is a fixed nondegenerate box.
The subdivision is the tensor product of equal coordinate partitions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N(h)=O(h^{-d})\) as \(h\downarrow0\), and complete \(m\)-way coordinate refinement has \(N_k=m^{dk}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Box-count growth for a specified isotropic tensor subdivision in fixed dimension.

source_refs.locator: Complexity Issues in Global Optimization: A Survey p. 27

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\prod_{i=1}^d[a_i,b_i]\subset\mathbb R^d\) be nondegenerate, let \(h>0\), and set \(n_i=\left\lceil(b_i-a_i)/h\right\rceil\). Partition coordinate interval \([a_i,b_i]\) into exactly \(n_i\) equal pieces. Every resulting coordinate interval has length at most \(h\), and the tensor subdivision contains exactly \[N(h)=\prod_{i=1}^d n_i=\prod_{i=1}^d\left\lceil\frac{b_i-a_i}{h}\right\rceil\] boxes. For fixed \(X\) and \(d\), \(N(h)=O(h^{-d})\) as \(h\downarrow0\). If every coordinate is instead divided into \(m\ge2\) equal pieces at each complete refinement level, then level \(k\) contains exactly \(m^{dk}\) boxes and its coordinate mesh is proportional to \(m^{-k}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The specified tensor partition uses the product of the coordinate ceiling counts, which grows on the order of h to the negative d; complete m-way coordinate refinement creates exactly m to the dk boxes at level k.
knowledge_statements.title: Subdivision Search Rate

source_witnesses.locator: Complexity Issues in Global Optimization: A Survey p. 27

children.title: Order-to-Rate Transfer
children.top_down_role: Structural connection between enclosure contraction quality and global-search progress.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subset\mathbb R^d\) is compact, \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) attains \(f_*=\min_{x\in X}f(x)\), and the finite active family \(\mathcal A_h\) covers \(X\).
For every \(B\in\mathcal A_h\), \(\operatorname{diam}(B)\le h\), \(L(B)\le\inf_{x\in B}f(x)\), and \(\inf_{x\in B}f(x)-L(B)\le C_Lh^p\).
The incumbent \(U\) is a feasible objective value satisfying \(0\le U-f_*\le C_Uh^p\), where \(p>0\) and \(C_L,C_U\ge0\).
Producing the exhaustive active cover at scale \(h\) uses \(O(h^{-d})\) boxes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(C_L+C_U>0\), \(U-\min_{B\in\mathcal A_h}L(B)\le(C_L+C_U)h^p\), and \(N(\varepsilon)=O(\varepsilon^{-d/p})\).

notation.meaning: common enclosure and incumbent error order
finite active box family at scale h
box count sufficient for certified gap epsilon

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer from uniform enclosure and incumbent error order to worst-case exhaustive box complexity.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47
Complexity Issues in Global Optimization: A Survey p. 27

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^d\) be compact, let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) attain \(f_*=\min_{x\in X}f(x)\), and let the finite active box family \(\mathcal A_h\) cover \(X\). Suppose every \(B\in\mathcal A_h\) has \(\operatorname{diam}(B)\le h\) and a validated lower bound \(L(B)\) satisfying \[0\le\inf_{x\in B}f(x)-L(B)\le C_Lh^p,\] where \(p>0\) and \(C_L\ge0\). Suppose also that a feasible incumbent value \(U\) satisfies \(0\le U-f_*\le C_Uh^p\), where \(C_U\ge0\). Then \[U-\min_{B\in\mathcal A_h}L(B)\le(C_L+C_U)h^p.\] If \(C_L+C_U>0\), it suffices to take \(h\le(\varepsilon/(C_L+C_U))^{1/p}\) to obtain certified gap at most \(\varepsilon>0\). If producing the exhaustive cover uses \(O(h^{-d})\) boxes, then the sufficient box complexity is \(N(\varepsilon)=O(\varepsilon^{-d/p})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A covering active family with uniform order-p lower-bound error and an order-p feasible incumbent yields an order-p certified gap; an h-to-the-negative-d subdivision count therefore becomes an epsilon-to-the-negative-d-over-p sufficient box bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Order-to-Rate Transfer

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

children.title: Rate Degradation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Dependency, nonsmoothness, and poor splitting regimes that weaken expected search progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Rate Degradation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complexity deterioration when effective error order is lower than the nominal enclosure order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume an exhaustive search retains a region of positive \(d\)-dimensional volume and uses boxes of diameter \(h\). Suppose its certified gap is \(\Theta(h^q)\) for some effective order \(q>0\), while covering the retained region requires \(\Theta(h^{-d})\) boxes. Achieving gap at most \(\varepsilon\) then requires \(h=\Theta(\varepsilon^{1/q})\) and \[N(\varepsilon)=\Theta(\varepsilon^{-d/q}).\] Thus if dependency, nonsmoothness, outward rounding, or a lower-order incumbent mechanism reduces a nominal order \(p\) to \(q<p\), the nominal rate \(\varepsilon^{-d/p}\) is not attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the effective gap order falls from p to q, exhaustive complexity degrades from epsilon to the negative d-over-p to negative d-over-q.

The certified gap is \(\Theta(h^q)\).
Covering requires \(\Theta(h^{-d})\) boxes.

children.title: Dimension-Driven Subdivision Growth
children.top_down_role: Combinatorial growth of box coverings under multidimensional refinement.

knowledge_statements.title: Dimension-Driven Subdivision Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential dependence on dimension under full coordinatewise subdivision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a \(d\)-dimensional box have initial coordinate mesh \(h_0\). If every refinement divides each coordinate into \(m\ge2\) equal parts, one parent produces \(m^d\) children. After \(k\) complete refinement levels, the partition has exactly \(m^{dk}\) boxes and mesh \(h_k=h_0m^{-k}\). Consequently, \[m^{dk}=\left(\frac{h_0}{h_k}\right)^d.\] For a fixed resolution ratio \(h_0/h_k>1\), the required box population grows exponentially with dimension \(d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full m-way refinement in every coordinate creates m to the d children per box and resolution-ratio to the d boxes overall.
assumptions_latex: \(d\ge1\) and \(m\ge2\).
Every box is refined in all coordinates at every level.

notation.meaning: number of equal pieces per coordinate and level

children.title: Contractor Cost–Effectiveness
children.top_down_role: Tradeoffs between contraction strength and per-box computational cost.

knowledge_statements.title: Contractor Cost–Effectiveness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Break-even condition in a per-box cost and surviving-box-count model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a search requiring \(N_0\) processed boxes without contraction, at baseline cost \(b>0\) per box. Suppose applying a contractor to every processed box adds cost \(c>0\) and reduces the processed population to \(N_C\). Under this additive cost model, contraction is computationally cost-effective exactly when \[(b+c)N_C<bN_0,\] equivalently when \[\frac{N_C}{N_0}<\frac{b}{b+c}.\] Equality is the break-even boundary; a smaller population reduction does not compensate for contractor cost in this model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contractor pays off precisely when its surviving-box fraction is below the baseline-cost fraction of total per-box cost.
assumptions_latex: Baseline processing costs \(b>0\) per box.
Contractor application adds \(c>0\) per processed box.
Costs are additive and box-independent.

children.title: Traversal-Dependent Storage Regimes
children.top_down_role: Memory behavior associated with depth-first, breadth-first, best-bound, or hybrid traversal.

knowledge_statements.title: Traversal-Dependent Storage Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Live-box storage for binary interval branch-and-bound under depth-first and best-bound traversal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be a binary subdivision tree explored to depth \(D\), and let \(W\) be the maximum number of generated, unprocessed leaves. With constant-size records, depth-first traversal with pending siblings stores at most \(D+1\) live boxes. A best-bound traversal that retains every active leaf stores the current frontier and therefore at most \(W\) live boxes; in the worst case \(W=\Theta(N)\), where \(N\) boxes have been generated. Thus traversal can change the storage upper bound from \(O(D)\) to \(O(N)\) without changing the validated pruning predicates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Depth-first traversal with pending siblings stores at most a number of live boxes proportional to the explored depth, whereas best-bound traversal may retain a frontier proportional to all generated boxes.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a finite binary subdivision tree.
Each live-box record occupies \(\Theta(1)\) memory.
Traversal does not discard boxes except through the same validated pruning rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_{\mathrm{DFS}}\le D+1\) and \(S_{\mathrm{best}}\le W=O(N)\), with worst-case \(W=\Theta(N)\).

children.title: Memory Exhaustion Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Search configurations in which retained regional state exceeds available storage.

knowledge_statements.title: Memory Exhaustion Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Capacity threshold for the live active-region set of a validated interval search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an implementation has usable memory \(M\), fixed non-box overhead \(b<M\), and requires at least \(s>0\) bytes for each live-box record. If the active frontier is \(\mathcal F\), a necessary condition for in-memory feasibility is \(b+s|\mathcal F|\le M\). Consequently, any traversal reaching \(|\mathcal F|>\lfloor(M-b)/s\rfloor\) must compress, externalize, reconstructibly remove, or validly prune records; otherwise it cannot remain within the memory budget. Thus \(\lfloor(M-b)/s\rfloor\) is an upper bound on feasible in-memory frontier cardinality. Removing an unresolved record without validated pruning, lossless reconstruction, or equivalent retained coverage can invalidate completeness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The active frontier cannot fit in memory once it exceeds the upper bound determined by the usable budget and minimum record size; unjustified removal of unresolved search state can invalidate completeness.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is the usable memory budget.
Every live record requires at least \(s>0\) bytes.
Unresolved boxes are necessary for search completeness unless validly pruned, losslessly reconstructible, or covered by equivalent retained state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\mathcal F|\le\left\lfloor(M-b)/s\right\rfloor\) is necessary for in-memory feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Boundary Box Explosion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary-covering lower bound when interval feasibility tests remain inconclusive near a regular constraint boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\) have a compact \(C^1\) boundary patch \(\Gamma\) of positive \((n-1)\)-dimensional measure. Consider shape-regular boxes of diameter at most \(h\) whose union covers \(\Gamma\). For sufficiently small \(h\), their number is at least \(c h^{-(n-1)}\) for some \(c>0\). Hence, if every box meeting \(\Gamma\) remains unresolved by the interval constraint test until diameter \(h\), a complete validated search must retain or process \(\Omega(h^{-(n-1)})\) boundary boxes.

Subdivision boxes are uniformly shape-regular.

knowledge_statements.title: Flat Objective Regions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of strict lower-bound pruning on a positive-size region attaining the global minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be the feasible set, let \(f^*=\min_{x\in K}f(x)\), and suppose \(f(x)=f^*\) on a set \(R\subset K\) with nonempty interior. For every box \(B\) meeting \(R\), any valid range enclosure \(F(B)\supseteq f(B\cap K)\) satisfies \(\inf F(B)\le f^*\). Even with an incumbent \(U=f^*\), the strict pruning test \(\inf F(B)>U\) cannot reject such a box. Exact branch-and-bound must therefore retain, subdivide, or separately certify the boxes covering \(R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Boxes intersecting a flat globally minimal region cannot be removed by strict lower-bound comparison, even when the optimal value is known.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) attains its global minimum \(f^*\) on \(K\).
\(R\subset K\) has nonempty interior and \(f|_R=f^*\).

children.title: Minimizer Isolation Boundaries

knowledge_statements.title: Minimizer Isolation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Topological criterion separating isolated global minimizers from accumulating minimizer families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(M_0=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in K}f(x)\), and let \(x^*\in M_0\). The minimizer \(x^*\) is isolated in \(M_0\) exactly when there exists \(r>0\) such that \(M_0\cap B_r(x^*)=\{x^*\}\). Isolation fails exactly when every \(r>0\) contains another global minimizer; equivalently, there is a sequence \((x_j)\subset M_0\setminus\{x^*\}\) with \(x_j\to x^*\). This failure is the boundary beyond which a certificate claiming a unique minimizer near \(x^*\) is false.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global minimizer is isolated precisely when some neighborhood contains no other global minimizer; failure produces distinct minimizers converging to it.

\(f\) attains its global minimum on \(K\).

children.title: Singular Constraint Manifolds

knowledge_statements.title: Singular Constraint Manifolds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of regular inverse-based validation at a rank-deficient equality-constrained solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuously differentiable and satisfy \(h(\bar x)=0\). If \(Dh(\bar x)\) is singular, then every interval matrix enclosure \([Dh](B)\) on a box \(B\ni\bar x\) contains a singular matrix. Consequently, no test whose validity requires every matrix in \([Dh](B)\) to be nonsingular can certify regularity on such a box. Standard inverse-based interval Newton or Krawczyk uniqueness hypotheses therefore fail at \(\bar x\), although alternative singular-root or constraint-specific certificates may still apply.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a rank-deficient equality solution, Jacobian enclosures contain a singular matrix, so regular inverse-based uniqueness tests cannot satisfy their hypotheses.

\(Dh(\bar x)\) is singular.

knowledge_statements.title: Dependency-Dominated Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact cancellation obscured by repeated-variable dependency in natural interval evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(f(x)=x-x\) on \(B=[a,b]\), with width \(w=b-a\). Thus the enclosure width is \(2w\) although the true range width is zero. If a validated decision requires enclosure radius at most \(\tau>0\), uniform bisection from initial width \(w_0\) needs at least \(\lceil\log_2(w_0/\tau)\rceil\) levels solely because of representation-induced dependency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For x minus x, natural interval arithmetic produces a nonzero enclosure, forcing refinement even though the true function is identically zero.

children.title: Cluster Effect
children.top_down_role: Repeated subdivision around isolated or clustered solutions that are insufficiently excluded from neighboring boxes.

knowledge_statements.title: Cluster Effect
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accumulation of unresolved neighboring boxes around solutions when exclusion loses effectiveness near the solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\) be the solution set and let \(E(B)\) be a validated exclusion predicate, where \(E(B)=\mathrm{true}\) implies \(B\cap Z=\varnothing\). A cluster effect occurs if there are pairwise distinct boxes \((B_j)\) with \(B_j\cap Z=\varnothing\), \(\operatorname{dist}(B_j,Z)\to0\), and \(E(B_j)=\mathrm{false}\). An exhaustive subdivision method cannot discard these boxes using \(E\); it must refine them or invoke a stronger certificate. If at least \(q_\ell\) such boxes occur at subdivision level \(\ell\), then at least \(\sum_{i=0}^{L}q_i\) unresolved-box visits occur through level \(L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The cluster effect arises when increasingly close solution-free boxes cannot be excluded, forcing repeated refinement around the solution set.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is sound but may be incomplete.
The boxes \(B_j\) are solution-free and approach \(Z\).
Search is exhaustive over boxes not excluded by a validated predicate.

knowledge_statements.title: Unsafe Heuristic Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A concrete loss of global validity caused by treating an unverified rejection as pruning.

Suppose a heuristic rejects \(B=[0,1/2]\) without a validated infeasibility certificate or a lower bound proving that \(B\) cannot improve the incumbent. The remaining region is \((1/2,1]\), whose infimum is \(1/2\); hence every reported point from the retained region has objective value strictly above \(f(x^*)=0\). Treating the heuristic rejection as validated pruning therefore invalidates both global optimality and completeness claims.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discarding the left half of a simple linear problem without a certificate removes its unique minimizer and invalidates global guarantees.

children.title: Range-Enclosure Certificates

knowledge_statements.title: Range-Enclosure Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Locally checkable evidence that recorded intervals contain all objective or constraint values on a box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a box \(B\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and mapping \(g:B\to\mathbb R^m\), a range-enclosure certificate is a record \(C=(B,G,\mathcal T)\), where \(G=G_1\times\cdots\times G_m\) is an interval box and \(\mathcal T\) is a reproducible trace of inclusion-valid operations with outward rounding. A verifier accepts \(C\) only if replaying \(\mathcal T\) from the recorded data yields an enclosure contained in \(G\). Acceptance certifies \(g(B)\subseteq G\); consequently, each component satisfies \(\inf G_i\le g_i(x)\le\sup G_i\) for every \(x\in B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A replayable outward-rounded computation certifies that every objective or constraint value on a box lies in the recorded interval enclosure.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is a represented interval box.
Every operation in \(\mathcal T\) is inclusion-valid and outward-rounded.
The verifier reproduces the stated enclosure from recorded data.

children.top_down_role: Shared computational graphs for range evaluation and contractor propagation.

knowledge_statements.title: Expression-Graph Interval Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward interval evaluation with optional solution-preserving backward contractor propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Process the nodes of \(G\) in topological order. Assign each variable leaf its component interval from \(X\), each constant leaf a containing point interval, and each operation node \(v\) the outward-rounded value \(Y_v=\Phi_v(Y_{p_1},\ldots,Y_{p_k})\). The root interval then satisfies \[\{F(x):x\in X\}\subseteq Y_r.\] If an output restriction \(R\) is imposed, intersect \(Y_r\) with \(R\) and apply the declared solution-preserving inverse contractors backward along the graph until a fixed point, emptiness, or a prescribed iteration limit is reached. For the resulting variable box \(X'\), every \(x\in X\) satisfying \(F(x)\in R\) remains in \(X'\); emptiness therefore certifies that no such point exists in \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate the expression graph forward with validated interval primitives to enclose every output over the input box. Optional solution-preserving backward contractors may reduce the variable box without removing any point satisfying the imposed output restriction.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite directed acyclic expression graph with root \(r\), representing \(F:X\to\mathbb{R}\) on a box \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
Each variable leaf is assigned its component interval from \(X\), and every primitive interval operator \(\Phi_v\) encloses its corresponding real operation.
Every inverse contractor used in the optional backward pass preserves all assignments satisfying its associated operation and the imposed output restriction \(R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{F(x):x\in X\}\subseteq Y_r\); after backward propagation, \(\{x\in X:F(x)\in R\}\subseteq X'\subseteq X\).

notation.meaning: Expression graph and its root node.
Required output range for backward propagation.
Variable box remaining after backward propagation.

children.title: Common-Subexpression Management
children.top_down_role: Representation choices balancing dependency, reuse, and propagation strength.

knowledge_statements.title: Common-Subexpression Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic sharing of repeated expression nodes under interval evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be the current variable box. Replacing repeated occurrences of the same real subexpression \(s(x)\), with identical variable bindings and domains, by one shared graph node preserves the represented point function. If that node is evaluated by an inclusion interval extension, its value \(Y_s\) satisfies \[\{s(x):x\in X\}\subseteq Y_s,\] so reusing \(Y_s\) at every consumer preserves enclosure validity. Sharing does not introduce a general correlation rule for independently defined interval variables, and algebraically equivalent but semantically different graph representations can yield enclosures of different widths or different contractor propagation behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated occurrences of the same subexpression may share one validated interval node without changing the represented function or invalidating its enclosure. Different algebraic graph representations can still produce different enclosure widths and contractor behavior.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is the current variable box.
Occurrences are merged only when they denote the same real-valued subexpression under identical variable bindings and domains.
Every primitive interval operator used by the graph is inclusion isotonic and encloses its real operation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Semantic sharing preserves the represented point function and enclosure validity, but algebraically equivalent graph representations need not produce equally narrow interval evaluations.

notation.meaning: A repeated real subexpression and its interval enclosure.

children.title: Symbolic-Interval Preprocessing Pipeline
children.top_down_role: Reformulation, simplification, scaling, and domain analysis before exhaustive search.

children.title: Symbolic Reformulation
children.top_down_role: Algebraic restructuring intended to improve validated model evaluation.

knowledge_statements.title: Symbolic Reformulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact extended reformulations suitable for validated interval processing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A symbolic reformulation is validation-compatible when it defines an extended feasible set \(\widetilde{\mathcal F}\subseteq X\times Y\) and objective \(\widetilde f\) such that, for every \(x\in X\), \[x\in\mathcal F\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \exists y\in Y\text{ with }(x,y)\in\widetilde{\mathcal F},\] and every such feasible extension satisfies \(\widetilde f(x,y)=f(x)\). Each introduced operation must have a validated interval extension on its declared domain, and all domain, sign, and branch constraints required by division, roots, logarithms, inverses, or piecewise operations must remain explicit. Under these conditions, feasibility and objective certificates for the extended model project to the original variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symbolic reformulation is validation-compatible when projection of its extended feasible set exactly recovers the original feasible set, every feasible extension preserves the objective value, and all introduced operations retain their required domain and branch constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is the original variable box, \(\mathcal F\subseteq X\) is the original feasible set, and \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is the original objective.

\(Y\subseteq\mathbb{R}^k\) is an auxiliary-variable domain, \(\widetilde{\mathcal F}\subseteq X\times Y\) is the extended feasible set, and \(\widetilde f:X\times Y\to\mathbb{R}\) is the extended objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in\mathcal F\) if and only if \(\exists y\in Y\) with \((x,y)\in\widetilde{\mathcal F}\), and every feasible extension satisfies \(\widetilde f(x,y)=f(x)\).

children.title: Expression Simplification
children.top_down_role: Removal or reduction of redundant expression structure before search.

assumptions_latex: Expressions \(e\) and \(e'\) are defined on a declared box \(X\).
The simplifier records all side conditions used by identities involving division, powers, roots, logarithms, or branches.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e(x)=e'(x)\) for every \(x\in X\) satisfying the recorded side conditions.

notation.meaning: Predicate collecting required domain and branch conditions.

review_flags: validated simplification rules require source confirmation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain-aware simplification before interval evaluation.

source_refs.locator: 1.2 Structure of Global Optimization Models p. 3
2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A simplification \(e\mapsto e'\) is admissible on \(X\) only if the system can establish \[\forall x\in X:\ S(x)\Longrightarrow\bigl(e(x)\text{ and }e'(x)\text{ are defined and }e(x)=e'(x)\bigr).\] If \(S\) is not certified throughout \(X\), the transformation must be rejected, the box must be split or contracted until \(S\) holds, or the side condition must remain explicitly in the model. Equality of point expressions guarantees semantic preservation but does not guarantee that the natural interval evaluations of \(e\) and \(e'\) have equal width.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simplification is valid only where both expressions are defined and every required sign, nonzero, and branch condition is certified. Equivalent expressions may still have different interval widths.
knowledge_statements.title: Expression Simplification

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2 Structure of Global Optimization Models p. 3
2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

children.title: Interval Domain Preprocessing
children.top_down_role: Validated analysis of domains, singularities, scaling, and admissible evaluation regions.

assumptions_latex: The current domain is a box \(X=\prod_{i=1}^n X_i\).
Each preprocessing rule is a validated contractor \(C_j\) satisfying \(C_j(X)\subseteq X\).
No contractor removes a point satisfying the original constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F\cap X\subseteq C(X)\subseteq X\), or \(C(X)=\varnothing\) certifies infeasibility of \(X\).

notation.meaning: Feasible set of the original constraints.

review_flags: contractor preprocessing procedure requires source confirmation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validated contraction and domain checks before branch-and-bound evaluation.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(X^{(0)}=X\). In a fixed or fair order, compute \(X^{(t+1)}=C_{j_t}(X^{(t)})\), including intersections with declared variable bounds and domains of division, roots, logarithms, and inverse functions. Stop and return infeasible if any component becomes empty. Otherwise stop at a fixed point, a certified contraction tolerance, or an iteration limit, and return \(C(X)=X^{(t)}\). Since each contractor preserves all feasible points, \[\mathcal F\cap X\subseteq C(X)\subseteq X;\] hence emptiness is a certificate that the original box contains no feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly apply validated contractors and operation-domain restrictions. The returned box contains every originally feasible point, while an empty result certifies that the input box is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Interval Domain Preprocessing

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

children.title: Reformulation Compatibility Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where symbolic changes alter enclosure quality or restrict validated applicability.

assumptions_latex: A proposed rewrite is pointwise valid only under a side condition \(S(x)\).
The current interval box \(X\) does not certify \(S(x)\) for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Applying the rewrite globally on \(X\) can change the feasible set, objective, or definedness and therefore cannot support a validated certificate.

notation.meaning: Side condition required by a rewrite.

review_flags: sharp reformulation boundaries require source confirmation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain, branch, and dependency limits of symbolic interval reformulation.

source_refs.locator: 1.2 Structure of Global Optimization Models p. 3
2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A rewrite cannot be used as a validated equivalence on \(X\) when its required condition \(S\) is not certified throughout \(X\). For example, replacing \(x/x\) by \(1\) fails on any \(X\) with \(0\in X\), because the original expression is undefined at \(x=0\); replacing \(\sqrt{x^2}\) by \(x\) fails when \(X\) contains negative values, because \(\sqrt{x^2}=|x|\). Such a rewrite becomes admissible only after retaining the necessary constraint, contracting or splitting \(X\) so the condition holds, or using a branch-aware equivalent representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rewrites fail validation when their nonzero, sign, domain, or branch conditions are not certified. Concrete examples include canceling x/x across zero and replacing absolute value by x across negative values.
knowledge_statements.title: Reformulation Compatibility Boundaries

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2 Structure of Global Optimization Models p. 3
