children.title: User-Supplied Enclosure Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Extension points for trusted model-specific range and derivative bounds.

assumptions_latex: A callback is invoked on a box \(X\subseteq D\) for a declared model quantity \(q:D\to\mathbb{R}^m\).
The callback uses specified outward-rounded arithmetic or returns independently checkable evidence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{q(x):x\in X\}\subseteq Q(X)\) is the required interface contract.

notation.meaning: Model-specific value, derivative, or range quantity.

review_flags: trusted extension interface requires source confirmation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contract for model-specific value and derivative enclosure callbacks.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every admissible input box \(X\subseteq D\), a user-supplied callback must either return an interval vector \(Q(X)\) satisfying \[\{q(x):x\in X\}\subseteq Q(X),\] return a checkable certificate from which this inclusion follows, or report that no enclosure is available. The declaration must identify the quantity enclosed, its domain, dimensions, parameter values, arithmetic semantics, and treatment of exceptional inputs. A solver may use \(Q(X)\) for pruning or certification only after validating this contract; an unchecked approximation may guide search but cannot justify exclusion or an optimality claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A user callback must return a valid enclosure, checkable evidence, or explicit failure, together with its domain and arithmetic semantics. Unchecked approximations cannot justify pruning or certification.
knowledge_statements.title: User-Supplied Enclosure Interfaces

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the interface leaf and is internally coherent, but its detailed callback contract, trust policy, certificate alternative, and permitted use for pruning are implementation-level claims not established by the cited general interval-methods locator. A source specifically documenting validated user-supplied enclosure interfaces is required.

children.title: Robust Validated Execution
children.top_down_role: Execution mechanisms addressing precision, exceptional operations, and long-running searches.

children.title: Precision Escalation
children.top_down_role: Selective higher precision for unresolved boxes and failed certificates.

assumptions_latex: The objective has a rigorous interval extension at every supported precision.
Each queued box carries its current enclosure and certificate status.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every discarded box remains justified by a certificate computed at a precision sufficient for that certificate.

notation.meaning: working precision assigned to box B
validated interval evaluation at precision p

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: directed-rounding interval solvers commonly retry unresolved evaluations at increasing precision
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selective escalation within a validated branch-and-bound search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an unresolved queue \(\mathcal Q\), initialize each box \(B\) with precision \(p(B)=p_0\). Compute \(F_{p(B)}(B)\) and attempt the required feasibility, contraction, or pruning certificate. If the certificate succeeds, record it and process \(B\) accordingly. If evaluation is finite but inconclusive, or a certificate fails because its interval margins contain zero, replace \(p(B)\) by a strictly larger supported precision and reevaluate without reusing uncertified bounds. Stop escalating when a certificate succeeds, a prescribed precision limit is reached, or subdivision is selected; in the latter two cases retain \(B\) as unresolved or bisect it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retry only unresolved boxes at higher precision, retaining a box unless a fresh rigorous evaluation produces a valid contraction, pruning, or feasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Precision Escalation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the Precision Escalation leaf and is mathematically conservative, but no source supports its escalation triggers, certificate handling, or stopping policy.

children.title: Rounding-Mode Isolation
children.top_down_role: Protection of interval kernels from uncontrolled floating-point state.

assumptions_latex: The interval kernel can set and restore the floating-point environment.
All interval endpoints are produced by directed rounding or an equivalent verified enclosure mechanism.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every interval returned by the isolated kernel encloses the corresponding exact real range independently of the caller's prior rounding mode.

notation.meaning: exact range of a real operation g over interval arguments X
interval returned by the protected kernel

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: validated floating-point interval kernels require controlled directed rounding and restoration of ambient state
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Isolation contract for mutable hardware or runtime rounding state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Rounding-mode isolation holds when each kernel invocation saves the caller's floating-point environment, establishes the rounding modes required for its lower and upper endpoint computations, prevents concurrent or nested code from altering that environment during those computations, and restores the saved environment on every normal or exceptional exit. For every supported real operation \(g\) and interval argument tuple \(X\), the returned interval \(G(X)\) must satisfy \(g(X)\subseteq G(X)\). No enclosure or certificate produced inside the invocation may depend on the rounding mode that was active before entry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A protected interval kernel controls and restores rounding state on every exit, so its enclosures remain valid regardless of caller state or concurrency.
knowledge_statements.title: Rounding-Mode Isolation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits Rounding-Mode Isolation, but the claims about nested or concurrent mutation, exceptional restoration, and caller-state independence require a source specifying the floating-point environment model.

children.title: Partial-Function Exception Semantics
children.top_down_role: Validated treatment of singularities, overflow, and restricted elementary-function domains.

children.title: Partial-Function Domains
children.top_down_role: Validated treatment of expressions defined only on restricted argument regions.

assumptions_latex: The real expression is interpreted compositionally from explicitly specified partial elementary operations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A box is directly evaluable exactly when it lies inside the expression's recursively defined real domain.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the domain of a composite partial function is defined recursively by operand domains and primitive-operation domains
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Real-domain semantics for interval evaluation of partial expressions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a primitive partial operation \(h:D_h\subseteq\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\), its domain is \(D_h\). Recursively, if \(f(x)=h(f_1(x),\ldots,f_m(x))\), then \[D_f=\{x:x\in\bigcap_{i=1}^m D_{f_i},\ (f_1(x),\ldots,f_m(x))\in D_h\}.\] An interval box \(B\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is directly evaluable for \(f\) only when \(B\subseteq D_f\). If \(B\cap D_f=\varnothing\), it contains no feasible point for a model requiring \(f\); if neither relation is certified, the box is domain-unresolved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The domain of a composite expression contains exactly the points where every subexpression is defined and every primitive receives an argument in its own domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Function Domains

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The recursive domain definition fits the leaf, but the conclusion says direct evaluability holds exactly when B is contained in the real domain, whereas the statement establishes only a necessary condition; dependency-sensitive interval evaluation may require additional qualifications.

children.title: Singularity Isolation
children.top_down_role: Regional handling of poles, branch boundaries, and undefined expression points.

assumptions_latex: The singular set can be enclosed or separated by validated predicates.
The optimization model excludes points where a required expression is undefined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No box is evaluated across an unresolved singularity, and only boxes certified disjoint from the admissible domain are discarded.

notation.meaning: domain of the partial expression f
singular set, the complement of the domain

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: validated subdivision separates boxes lying inside, outside, or across the domain boundary of a partial expression
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subdivision-based isolation of domain singularities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each box \(B\), apply validated domain predicates to classify it. If \(B\subseteq D_f\), evaluate \(f\) using its interval extension. If \(B\cap D_f=\varnothing\), discard \(B\) only when the model requires membership in \(D_f\), recording the domain-exclusion certificate. Otherwise \(B\) intersects or may intersect \(S_f\); do not use an interval value obtained by crossing that unresolved singular set. Instead contract \(B\) with domain constraints or bisect it, and repeat classification on the children. A child that cannot yet be classified remains unresolved rather than being pruned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classify boxes relative to the expression domain; evaluate interior boxes, certify and discard exterior boxes, and subdivide boxes that may cross a singularity.
knowledge_statements.title: Singularity Isolation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm matches Singularity Isolation and conservatively retains unclassified boxes, but its classification and exclusion protocol has no cited support.

children.title: Overflow Exception Handling
children.top_down_role: Validated responses to range overflow during interval evaluation.

assumptions_latex: Finite endpoint overflow is detectable by the interval arithmetic implementation.
An extended-real interval representation or higher-precision fallback is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Overflow can weaken a bound but cannot create an unsound finite enclosure or justify pruning by itself.

notation.meaning: exact range of the evaluated expression over B

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: validated arithmetic must convert overflow into conservative extended bounds or retry at greater range
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conservative response to endpoint overflow during validated evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When an endpoint operation overflows, the evaluator must not retain a wrapped, saturated finite, or non-numeric endpoint as a certified bound. It shall either recompute the operation in a format with greater exponent range or replace the affected lower endpoint by \(-\infty\), the affected upper endpoint by \(+\infty\), or both, so that \(f(B)\subseteq F(B)\) remains true. Any pruning or contraction test requiring the lost finite bound is then inconclusive. The box is retained for precision escalation, reformulation, or subdivision unless an independent validated certificate disposes of it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Treat overflow as loss of information: retry with greater range or use infinite endpoints, and never prune using a bound destroyed by overflow.
knowledge_statements.title: Overflow Exception Handling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits Overflow Exception Handling, but the permitted responses to endpoint overflow and their enclosure guarantees depend on the arithmetic representation and require an authoritative implementation or interval-arithmetic source.

children.title: Indeterminate Evaluation Recovery
children.top_down_role: Conservative continuation or subdivision following unresolved numerical exceptions.

assumptions_latex: The evaluator distinguishes undefined operations, overflow, and enclosure-preserving extended results.
Subdivision and precision escalation preserve the original feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Recovery either produces a fresh validated enclosure or returns unresolved subboxes; it never turns an indeterminate result into an unsupported certificate.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: validated solvers recover from indeterminate forms by dependency-aware reformulation, increased precision, or subdivision
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery from undefined or non-informative interval evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If evaluation of \(f\) on \(B\) produces an indeterminate form, first classify its cause. For a removable dependency artifact, reevaluate an algebraically equivalent validated form; for insufficient precision, escalate precision; for a box spanning incompatible branches or a singular boundary, bisect or apply domain contraction. Accept a recovered interval only after a fresh inclusion check establishes that it encloses every defined value \(f(x)\) for \(x\in B\cap D_f\). If all permitted recovery steps fail, mark \(B\) unresolved. An indeterminate value alone is neither a feasibility certificate nor a pruning certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classify an indeterminate evaluation, then reformulate, raise precision, or subdivide; accept only a fresh enclosure and otherwise retain the region as unresolved.
knowledge_statements.title: Indeterminate Evaluation Recovery

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The recovery algorithm fits the leaf and avoids unsupported pruning, but no source establishes the stated cause classification, permitted reformulations, or fresh inclusion-check requirement.

children.title: Validated Restart Persistence
children.top_down_role: Persistence of exhaustive-search state and certificate provenance.

children.title: Search-State Checkpoints
children.top_down_role: Persistent snapshots of unresolved regions, certified bounds, and traversal metadata.

assumptions_latex: Every queued region has a stable identifier and a rigorously computed bound.
Checkpoint serialization preserves interval endpoints exactly or outwardly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Restoring the checkpoint reconstructs a search frontier whose union contains every region unresolved at checkpoint time.

notation.meaning: union of boxes in a queue

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: restartable branch-and-bound checkpoints must preserve the unresolved frontier and its validated metadata
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent representation of the unresolved branch-and-bound frontier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A search-state checkpoint is a tuple \(C_s=(\mathcal Q_c,U_c,R_c,V_c)\), where \(\mathcal Q_c\) stores every unresolved box with its validated lower bound, precision, and processing status; \(U_c\) is the current certified incumbent bound; \(R_c\) records deterministic reconstruction data such as pending ownership or subdivision ancestry; and \(V_c\) identifies the arithmetic and model semantics. Serialization must preserve each box outwardly and must not increase a stored lower bound or decrease \(U_c\) unless the replacement is independently certified. A restored queue must cover \(|\mathcal Q_c|\), including work that was in flight when the checkpoint became committed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A search checkpoint stores the complete unresolved frontier, rigorous bounds, incumbent, reconstruction metadata, and arithmetic semantics without narrowing any saved region.
knowledge_statements.title: Search-State Checkpoints

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits Search-State Checkpoints, but completeness for in-flight work, outward serialization, and the monotonic bound restrictions are substantive persistence invariants without cited evidence.

children.title: Certificate-State Checkpoints
children.top_down_role: Persistent snapshots of accumulated certificate artifacts and provenance.

assumptions_latex: Every pruning, contraction, and incumbent claim has reproducible validated premises.
Checkpoint serialization preserves directed bounds conservatively.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each restored claim is either revalidated from saved premises or withdrawn before it can affect the resumed search.

notation.meaning: claim and validated premises of certificate k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: persistent validation requires certificate claims to retain replayable premises and semantic version data
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent evidence supporting decisions already committed by the search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A certificate-state checkpoint stores \(C_v=(\mathcal C_c,V_c)\), where every record \(k\in\mathcal C_c\) contains a claim \(q_k\), its box or point, validated premises \(P_k\), the incumbent version used, and the arithmetic semantics \(V_c\). On restoration, a verifier recomputes or checks \(P_k\Rightarrow q_k\) under compatible semantics. A pruning certificate is reusable only if its incumbent premise is no weaker than the restored certified incumbent; a contraction certificate must identify the parent region it covers. Any record failing verification is withdrawn, and the affected region is returned to the unresolved search state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certificate checkpoint stores replayable claims, premises, regions, incumbent versions, and arithmetic semantics; failed revalidation returns affected regions to the search.
knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-State Checkpoints

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role fits the leaf, but the checkpoint schema and replay rules are unsupported. The phrase 'incumbent premise is no weaker' also needs a precise inequality or version-order definition before the reuse condition is reliable.

children.title: Validated Restart
children.top_down_role: Resumption of exhaustive search from a checked persistent state.

assumptions_latex: A committed search-state checkpoint and its matching certificate-state checkpoint are available.
The restored arithmetic and model semantics pass compatibility checks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resumed computation preserves all previously certified exclusions and retains every region not covered by a valid certificate.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a validated restart must atomically restore the frontier and revalidate every persisted decision used after restart
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restart protocol preserving validated branch-and-bound coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Load the latest jointly committed search and certificate checkpoints. Verify their model, expression, arithmetic, and checkpoint-version identifiers; reject the restart if compatibility cannot be established. Reconstruct \(\mathcal Q_r\), outwardly enclosing all saved boxes and recovering interrupted work. Revalidate every certificate in \(\mathcal C_r\); return any region supported only by a failed certificate to \(\mathcal Q_r\). Revalidate the incumbent point before using \(U_r\), weakening \(U_r\) to \(+\infty\) if necessary. Resume processing only after the restored queue, incumbent, and certificates form one consistent committed state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restore one compatible committed state, recover interrupted boxes, revalidate certificates and the incumbent, and resume only after frontier coverage is consistent.
knowledge_statements.title: Validated Restart

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits Validated Restart and is conservatively stated, but atomic checkpoint pairing, compatibility checks, certificate recovery, and incumbent weakening require a dedicated validated-restart source.

children.title: Restart Continuity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Compatibility limits involving arithmetic environments, model versions, or incomplete state.

assumptions_latex: Checkpoint commitment and work processing may overlap.
Only durably committed records are available after a failure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any region crossing the continuity boundary is either durably unresolved or covered by a durable, revalidatable certificate, but never silently lost.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: crash consistency requires atomic ownership transfer between unresolved work and durable certificate state
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Crash-consistency boundary between durable and volatile search decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The restart continuity boundary is the atomic commitment of generation \(g\). For every box \(B\) represented before that boundary, generation \(g\) must contain either an unresolved record covering \(B\) or a durable certificate covering the portion removed from it. A failure between deleting \(B\) from the queue and committing its replacement children or certificate violates continuity and may lose feasible points. Duplicate recovery is admissible because it repeats work; omission is not. Mutable state created after generation \(g\) may be discarded only when all regions it owned are recoverable from generation \(g\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a crash boundary, every prior region must remain durably queued or durably certified; duplicate recovery is acceptable, but omission can invalidate global guarantees.
knowledge_statements.title: Restart Continuity Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind is appropriate, but the atomic-generation model and durable ownership invariant are specialized crash-consistency claims with no supporting citation.

children.title: Parallel Interval Search Interface
children.top_down_role: Certification-preserving concurrency mechanisms without duplicating general parallel branch-and-bound theory.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Interval Analysis: Parallel Methods for Global Optimization

children.title: Parallel Box Processing
children.top_down_role: Concurrent validated evaluation, contraction, and pruning of independent regions.

assumptions_latex: Each box operation uses inclusion-preserving interval arithmetic.
Queue removal and insertion are linearizable, and pruning reads a certified incumbent version.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Parallel execution preserves frontier coverage and the validity of every committed pruning decision.

notation.meaning: validated lower bound for box B

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concurrent validated branch-and-bound over independently owned boxes.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(\mathcal Q\) with the initial box and a certified incumbent \(U\). A worker atomically claims \(B\in\mathcal Q\), computes validated evaluations, contracts \(B\), and derives \(L(B)\). It may discard \(B\) only when a certificate proves infeasibility or \(L(B)\ge U_v-\varepsilon\) for a certified incumbent version \(U_v\). Otherwise it atomically publishes the contracted box or a covering set of children. Incumbent updates are published only after validating a feasible point. Termination requires an empty queue and no in-flight box; the output is the incumbent together with all accumulated certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers independently validate boxes, but atomic ownership, certified incumbent versions, covering child publication, and in-flight accounting preserve correctness and termination.
knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Box Processing

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits Parallel Box Processing, but the cited interval-global-optimization section does not specifically support linearizable queue ownership, incumbent versions, covering publication, in-flight accounting, or parallel termination. A dedicated parallel validated-search source is required.

children.title: Validated Incumbent Sharing

assumptions_latex: Every proposed incumbent point is checked by validated feasibility tests.
The objective value at an accepted point has a rigorous upper enclosure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every shared incumbent value is a valid global upper bound, and stale larger values can only delay pruning.

notation.meaning: rigorous upper endpoint of the objective enclosure at x

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: parallel minimization may safely share only certified monotonically improving incumbent upper bounds
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone publication of certified feasible objective upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization, a worker may propose \((x,\overline F(x))\) only after certifying that \(x\) satisfies every constraint and that \(f(x)\le\overline F(x)\). Publication performs the atomic update \(U\leftarrow\min\{U,\overline F(x)\}\) and associates \(U\) with the supporting feasibility and objective certificates. A worker may prune using a value it has read only through a valid bound comparison; it must record or recheck the incumbent version required by that certificate. Because published values never increase, using a stale larger \(U\) may miss pruning but cannot cause an invalid pruning decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers publish only certified feasible objective upper bounds through an atomic minimum; stale larger bounds reduce efficiency but do not compromise correctness.
knowledge_statements.title: Validated Incumbent Sharing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits Validated Incumbent Sharing, and monotone atomic minimum publication is plausible for minimization, but the certification and version-recording protocol has no cited support.

children.title: Unresolved-Region Queue Coordination
children.top_down_role: Shared management of pending regional search work.

knowledge_statements.title: Unresolved-Region Queue Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Atomic coordination protocol for parallel validated branch-and-bound on a minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\) contain unprocessed boxes and let \(W\) contain boxes exclusively owned by workers. Initialize \(Q=\{B_0\}\), \(W=\varnothing\), and a certified feasible upper bound \(U\). A worker atomically transfers one box \(B\) from \(Q\) to \(W\), computes an outward-rounded lower bound \(L(B)\), and either discards \(B\) when \(L(B)\ge U-\varepsilon\), or partitions it into children whose union contains \(B\) and atomically inserts the children into \(Q\). The worker then removes \(B\) from \(W\). Feasible improvements update \(U\) by an atomic minimum operation. Termination is declared only from an atomic snapshot satisfying \(Q=\varnothing\) and \(W=\varnothing\); the output is the incumbent and the accumulated pruning certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers atomically claim, process, split, and retire boxes; feasible incumbents are shared by atomic minimum, and termination requires both the queue and in-flight set to be empty.
assumptions_latex: Every computed \(L(B)\) is a certified lower bound on \(B\).
Every incumbent value \(U\) is attained by a feasible point.
Queue, ownership, incumbent, and termination operations are linearizable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No unresolved box is lost or processed concurrently by two workers, and empty-state termination accounts for every generated box.

notation.meaning: Queued and currently worker-owned boxes, respectively.
Certified lower bound for box B.
Certified incumbent value and requested absolute tolerance.

review_flags: Exact parallel queue protocol is not supported by the supplied textbook locators.
REQUEST_SOURCES for validated parallel branch-and-bound termination and ownership semantics.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits this protocol-oriented leaf, and the notation and delimited LaTeX are internally coherent. However, no source is cited for the claimed linearizable ownership protocol, atomic empty-state termination, or accumulated pruning certificate. The inventory's general interval-optimization sections do not support these concurrency-specific guarantees.

children.title: Bound-Queue Consistency
children.top_down_role: Consistency between incumbent updates, pruning decisions, and queued regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Queue Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency invariant connecting queued boxes, certified bounds, and the shared incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization, a queue state is bound-consistent when every entry \((B,\ell,v)\) satisfies \(\ell\le \inf_{x\in B\cap F}f(x)\), where \(v\) identifies the bound computation, and every removal is recorded as either processing or certified pruning. Pruning against an incumbent snapshot \(U_s\) is permitted only when \(U_s\) is a certified feasible value and \(\ell\ge U_s-\varepsilon\). Replacing \(U_s\) by a later incumbent \(U_t\le U_s\) may create additional pruning opportunities but cannot invalidate an earlier pruning decision. Priority keys may be stale, but they must not be substituted for the certified value \(\ell\) in the pruning test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each queued lower bound must remain certified, and pruning may use only a feasible incumbent snapshot; stale priorities may affect order but never justify deletion.
assumptions_latex: The feasible set is \(F\subseteq B_0\), and the task is \(\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\).
Shared incumbent updates are monotone: \(U_{t+1}\le U_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every pruned box satisfies \(\inf_{x\in B\cap F}f(x)\ge U_s-\varepsilon\), so its removal preserves the requested global guarantee.

notation.meaning: Queue entry comprising a box, certified lower bound, and version tag.
Certified incumbent snapshot used by a pruning decision.

review_flags: Supplied locators cover interval global optimization but not concurrent bound-queue invariants.
REQUEST_SOURCES for versioned queue consistency in parallel validated search.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the leaf, and the monotonic-incumbent argument is plausible for minimization. No cited source supports the version-tagged queue invariant, the required removal accounting, or the distinction between stale priority keys and certified pruning bounds. A source with a specific parallel validated-search locator is required.

children.title: Stale-State Coordination Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Effects of delayed incumbent propagation or obsolete queue information.

knowledge_statements.title: Stale-State Coordination Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates harmless stale reads from stale-state uses that can destroy validation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose incumbent values decrease monotonically and certified box lower bounds remain valid independently of scheduling. Reading an older incumbent \(U_s\ge U_t\) is safe for the pruning test \(L(B)\ge U_s-\varepsilon\), although it may delay pruning. Likewise, a stale priority affects efficiency only. Validation can fail if a worker prunes using an uncommitted value smaller than every certified feasible incumbent, if a box is deleted without durable transfer of ownership, or if termination uses a queue snapshot while some worker can still publish children. Thus stale observations are admissible only when they weaken pruning or alter order; they are inadmissible when they strengthen a certificate, lose work, or conceal in-flight work.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Old feasible incumbents and priorities can waste work safely; uncommitted stronger bounds, lost ownership transfers, or termination that ignores in-flight children can invalidate the result.
assumptions_latex: For every active box \(B\), \(L(B)\le\inf_{x\in B\cap F}f(x)\).
Certified incumbent snapshots satisfy \(U_s\ge U_t\ge f^*\) whenever \(s<t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Staleness preserves validation precisely when its use cannot remove a box that the corresponding current certified state would retain.

notation.meaning: Earlier and later certified incumbent values.
Certified lower bound over box B.

review_flags: The precise stale-state safety boundary requires a source on asynchronous validated branch-and-bound.
No supplied locator directly addresses concurrent termination or ownership failures.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind is appropriate. The examples of harmless and unsafe staleness are plausible, but the conclusion presents a precise boundary without evidence addressing asynchronous incumbent reads, ownership transfer, child publication, and distributed termination. The listed general textbooks do not directly establish that boundary.

children.title: Parallel Scheduling Reliability Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Irregular workload, order sensitivity, and reproducible validated outcomes.

children.title: Parallel Load Balancing
children.top_down_role: Distribution of irregular regional workloads across processing resources.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Load Balancing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validation-preserving work distribution by exclusive ownership and atomic work stealing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain one deque \(Q_i\) per worker and an in-flight ownership set \(W\). Initially, \(B_0\) belongs to exactly one deque. Worker \(i\) removes a local box, atomically records its ownership in \(W\), and performs validated bounding, pruning, or subdivision. When \(Q_i\) is empty, it steals an unowned box from another deque by an atomic remove-and-transfer operation. Generated children are published only after their complete interval data and certified bounds are visible. A processed parent leaves \(W\) only after all retained children have been published. The computation stops when every deque and \(W\) are empty under a termination-detection protocol; load-balancing choices affect placement and order but not certification tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers use local queues and atomic stealing, publish complete child records before retiring parents, and terminate only after all queues and ownership records are empty.
assumptions_latex: Each generated child family covers its parent box.
Deque transfers and ownership changes are atomic.
Interval evaluations use directed outward rounding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every unresolved box has exactly one queue or worker owner, so redistribution cannot duplicate, lose, or uncertifiably prune search regions.

notation.meaning: Local unresolved-box deque of worker i.
Set of boxes currently owned by workers.

review_flags: Load-balancing protocol is more specific than the supplied interval-method locator.
REQUEST_SOURCES for validated parallel work stealing and distributed termination.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the load-balancing leaf. The proposed deque, ownership, publication, and termination protocol is substantially more specific than ordinary interval branch-and-bound and has no citation. Evidence is required for validation-preserving work stealing and the claimed exactly-one-owner invariant.

children.title: Validated Outcome Reproducibility
children.top_down_role: Consistency of certified conclusions across parallel executions.

knowledge_statements.title: Validated Outcome Reproducibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reproducibility of certified guarantees, distinguished from identical execution traces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider two terminating runs on the same initial box, objective, constraints, tolerance, and outward-rounded interval operations. If each run partitions boxes by covering subdivisions, prunes only by certified infeasibility or the test \(L(B)\ge U-\varepsilon\), and accounts for every queued or in-flight box at termination, then each reported incumbent \(U_r\) satisfies \(f^*\le U_r\le f^*+\varepsilon\). Consequently, scheduling may change the visited boxes, final incumbent point, and certificate decomposition without changing validity at tolerance \(\varepsilon\). Equality of bit patterns, traces, or incumbent points requires additional deterministic arithmetic, tie-breaking, and reduction rules and is not implied by validated execution alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Different schedules may produce different traces and incumbent points, yet every correctly terminated run reproduces the same certified tolerance guarantee; bitwise identity needs stronger determinism.
assumptions_latex: Both runs use the same problem data and tolerance \(\varepsilon\).
All interval bounds and feasibility decisions are mathematically certified.
Both runs terminate with complete queue and in-flight accounting.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For each run \(r\), the output obeys \(0\le U_r-f^*\le\varepsilon\), although generally \(U_1\ne U_2\).

notation.meaning: Certified incumbent returned by run r.

review_flags: The supplied sources do not directly establish schedule-independent validation for parallel interval search.
REQUEST_SOURCES distinguishing certificate reproducibility from bitwise reproducibility.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the leaf, but the stated hypotheses do not explicitly say that termination occurs only after all unresolved queued and in-flight boxes have been exhausted or validly pruned; merely accounting for them is not sufficient for the epsilon-optimality conclusion. No source is supplied to resolve the intended termination condition or support schedule-independent certificate validity, so the reliable mathematical formulation remains source-dependent.

children.title: Deterministic Scheduling Regimes
children.top_down_role: Parallel scheduling configurations designed to stabilize processing order.

knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Scheduling Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient conditions for replayable parallel interval-search traces and outputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A scheduling regime is deterministic when unresolved boxes have a strict total order \(\prec\) determined solely by immutable box data; dequeue and work-publication events are committed in that order; subdivision, interval evaluation, and feasibility tests are deterministic; and simultaneous incumbent candidates are reduced by a fixed total order on value-point pairs. Termination detection must also observe the same committed event sequence. Under identical problem data, worker count, arithmetic environment, and tolerance, these conditions determine the same sequence of committed queue states and incumbent values. Merely assigning fixed worker identifiers or using a deterministic local priority rule is insufficient if completion timing can change the global commit order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replayable results require a global box order, deterministic computations and reductions, and ordered commits; deterministic local queues alone do not neutralize timing differences.
assumptions_latex: The initial state and worker count are identical between runs.
Arithmetic operations and outward-rounding modes are reproducible.
Every scheduling tie has a data-independent, fixed tie-breaker.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any two executions satisfying the regime produce identical committed search traces and identical reported certificates.

notation.meaning: Strict total order on unresolved boxes.
Incumbent candidate consisting of objective value and feasible point.

review_flags: This sufficient determinism regime lacks direct support in the supplied global-optimization locators.
REQUEST_SOURCES for reproducible parallel branch-and-bound scheduling.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind is suitable for a sufficient deterministic scheduling regime, and the statement distinguishes global commit order from local determinism. Nevertheless, the implication to identical committed traces and certificates has no supporting citation, particularly for concurrent publication, deterministic interval arithmetic, reduction ordering, and termination detection.

children.title: Order-Sensitivity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Variability in search traces, resource use, or certificate artifacts caused by execution order.

knowledge_statements.title: Order-Sensitivity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between schedule-dependent performance and schedule-dependent mathematical validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let two unresolved boxes \(B_1\) and \(B_2\) have equal priority, and suppose processing \(B_1\) first discovers a certified incumbent \(U_1<U_0\) that permits immediate pruning of \(B_2\). Reversing the order may therefore increase node count and produce a different subdivision tree. Nevertheless, if every lower bound is certified, every incumbent is feasible, queue ownership is complete, and pruning uses an atomic certified snapshot, either order preserves the final tolerance guarantee. Order becomes correctness-relevant when a race changes directed rounding, exposes a partially written bound, loses a box, accepts an infeasible incumbent, or permits premature termination. Thus scheduling order may control cost and representation, but only violations of validation invariants may control validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Processing order can change node counts and trees without changing correctness; it threatens validity only through rounding, publication, ownership, feasibility, or termination races.
assumptions_latex: The minimization search begins with certified incumbent \(U_0\).
Processing \(B_1\) can produce a feasible value \(U_1<U_0\).
Certified pruning uses \(L(B)\ge U-\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Changing the order of \(B_1\) and \(B_2\) may change work but not the certified result unless the ordering race violates a validation invariant.

notation.meaning: Unresolved boxes with equal scheduling priority.
Certified lower bound for a box.

review_flags: The concrete parallel order-sensitivity boundary is unsupported by the supplied textbook locators.
REQUEST_SOURCES for race safety and order dependence in validated interval search.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind matches the leaf, and the two-box example plausibly illustrates performance sensitivity to processing order. The broader assertion that order affects validity only through the enumerated validation-invariant violations is not supported by a cited source. A specific source on asynchronous validated branch-and-bound race safety and termination is required.
